About the Role :

Floor Interior Services is seeking a highly organized and customer-focused Project Coordinator (PC) to join our team at Floor Interior Services. In this role, you'll serve as the bridge between customers, our retail partner, and installers; ensuring projects are completed with accuracy, efficiency, and outstanding service.

Our ideal candidate is proactive, empathetic, and thrives in a fast-paced environment. You'll be the communicator, problem-solver, and coordinator who keeps everything moving smoothly from start to finish.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Schedule installations and confirm daily appointments with customers.
  • Track and monitor installation progress and service calls.
  • Act as the first point of contact via phone, email, and text for customers, our retail partner, and installers.
  • Guide installers in the field to ensure high-quality project delivery.
  • Assist in resolving customer concerns including site visits when needed.
  • Document and maintain accurate records of interactions, accounts, and project updates.
  • Identify customer needs, provide timely solutions , and follow up to ensure satisfaction.
  • Escalate store or project issues when appropriate.
  • Deliver service with urgency, professionalism, and attention to detail.
Skills & Qualifications:

  • 1-3 years of experience in a project coordination or customer service role.
  • Strong organizational and problem-solving abilities.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to multitask, prioritize, and manage time effectively.
  • Proficient with Microsoft Office (Outlook, Excel, Word, Teams).
  • High school diploma or equivalent required.
  • Customer service background a must.
  • Bilingual (English/Spanish) highly preferred.
  • Knowledge of the flooring industry is a plus.
  • Must possess a valid Florida Driver's License.
  • Must possess a current Forklift Certification or be willing to obtain one.
Why join Floor Interior Services?

For over 20 years, Floor Interior Services has been a trusted leader in delivering high-quality interior solutions. We take pride not only in our craftsmanship, but in our commitment to customer satisfaction and the growth of our employees and installers.

As part of our team, you'll have the opportunity to make a real impact; helping customers transform their spaces while building a rewarding career in a supportive environment.

Apply today and take the next step in your project coordinator career.

title: Shift Supervisor
description:
Shift Supervisor

The Tim Hortons Shift Supervisor position is operational in nature and involves the supervision of team member activities on shift to ensure that standards around people, product, cleanliness, and Exceptional Guest Experience are fulfilled.

People Management

  • Leads by example and demonstrates the importance of treating every team member and guest with respect
  • Assists the Restaurant Manager in recruitment and retention strategies
  • Reacts immediately to issues requiring attention during the shift
  • Provides ongoing, specific direction to team members
  • Encourages an exciting and fun work environment while motivating team members to meet goals
  • Trains, orientates and monitors new team members, using PTS and feedback binder
  • Reports to Restaurant Owner, General Manager, Manager and/or Assistant Manager on team member performance (positive or negative)
  • Assists in ensuring optimal team member coverage at all times and works various positions during busy periods to maintain optimal service levels through demonstrated floor leadership

Hospitality Management

  • Leads by example to demonstrate that the guest is top priority and reinforces positive hospitality behaviors with team members
  • Responds to guest in a friendly manner while maintaining an appropriate sense of urgency
  • Responds to guest service complaints in a timely manner, resolving problems and turning potentially negative situations into positive situations
  • Assists in the running of company-wide incentive programs

Operations Management

  • Displays knowledge of and works in compliance with applicable legislation
  • Complies with and enforces all Tim Hortons operating standards
  • Ensures that all product and packaging is properly merchandised and stocked
  • Responsible for shift cash procedures
  • Maintains operational efficiency through use of positioning charts
  • Supervises team members to ensure primary and secondary duties are completed
  • Ensures all restaurant policies are followed during the shift (e.g. cash policies, meal and break policies, food safety policies)
  • Keeps current on all new information on Portal or available through Townhall meetings
  • Assists the Restaurant Manager in driving sales and transactions during their shift
  • Completes all required shift documentation (e.g. records waste, mgr. walk thru, pre-rush checklists etc.)
  • Escalates to management any issues and/or problems

Health & Safety

  • Works in compliance with the occupational health and safety legislation
  • Knows, understands and follows safe work practices and procedures
  • Uses or wears personal protective equipment or clothing as required
  • Reports all injuries/illness, accidents, unsafe conditions, security incidents and any contravention of health and safety legislation, policies and procedures to the Restaurant Manager or Owner
  • Does not operate any equipment, machine, device or thing, or otherwise work in a manner that will endanger anyone
  • Ensures health and safety policies are followed during the shift including documentation and reporting of any work related injuries or accidents

Postural & Physical Demands Requirements

  • Frequent reaching above waist, chest, and shoulder level, as well as below waist level
  • Frequent to continuous need for manual dexterity of both hands (handling, gripping, fine finger control, etc.)
  • Continuous standing on tiled surfaces for all tasks
  • Ability to stand for long periods of time without a break
  • Frequent hip flexion while walking for all tasks
  • Occasional lifting of boxes of supplies/products weighing from <5 – 50 lbs. vertically from floor to knuckle height
  • Occasional lifting of milk crates weighing between 5 – 30 lbs. vertically from floor to knuckle height, knuckle to shoulder height, or from fridge to counter height
  • Frequent exposure to cold/below freezing and high heat temperatures (walk-in refrigerator and freezers, ovens)


*Must be 16 years of age or older.

title: Residential Coordinator
description:
DePaul Community Resources is recruiting for a Residential Coordinator – full-time (37.5-hour workweek) – Amelia, VA.
JOB SUMMARY:
The Residential Coordinator is a case manager and advocate, providing quality services that best meet the individual's social, health, community, and safety interests. The Residential Coordinator provides advocacy and case management for services based on the individual's interests, needs, and abilities. This position provides oversight to the sponsored residential home and provides support services to individuals on their assigned caseload. The Residential Coordinator also provides ongoing assessment of risk and protective factors and assesses the strengths and needs of providers and individuals served. This position is assigned to an on-call rotation.
SUPERVISION RECEIVED AND EXERCISED:
The Residential Coordinator reports directly to the Sponsored Residential Manager.
ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS AND DUTIES:
This list is not an exhaustive & all-inclusive list of job responsibilities. The distribution of time allotted for any function or duty is subject to change with or without notice. Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign other responsibilities to this job or reassign them elsewhere at any time.
Home Visit Compliance:
Conduct monthly home visits and two annual unannounced home visits to ensure the individual's needs are met, provided services are in accordance with approved person-centered and physical dwelling remains in compliance and free of safety concerns; weekly contacts for children (ages 18 and younger) in provider homes are required as outline in DBHDS regulation12VAC35-105-1235 and complies with DSS.
Individual Needs Assessment:
Attend individual's served appointments, conduct interviews, and monthly observational assessments to assess individual's health & safety needs (e.g., psychosocial, nutritional, medical, education, physical injuries, etc.).
Develop and implement person-centered plans (PCP) in accordance with regulations to appropriately meet individual's best interests; follow up with quarterly reviews to monitor ongoing needs and revise PCP if necessary to satisfy individual's best interests.
Inspection Compliance:
Upon inspections, ensures provider homes abide by 1) DBHDS and DMAS standards; 2) program policies and procedures and Human Rights; 3) develops corrective action plans to maintain compliance and safety throughout all areas of the home and buildings when necessary; conducts a minimum of two inspections at six-month intervals or as needed.
Reporting:
Attend staff meetings and medical appointments; follow through with suggestions for all involved parties; participate in home finder meetings as the Senior Residential Manager or Program Director schedules.
Inform appropriate parties (e.g., immediate supervisor, CSB Support Coordinator, guardian, in-service providers, day support, DSS, transportation, etc.) of significant events concerning the individual, such as, but not limited to, substance count discrepancies, suspected abuse/neglect, or serious incidents.
Promotes a positive work environment with positive relationships with sponsored home providers, parents, coworkers, referral agencies, community partners, respite, and backup providers; monthly contact with appropriate parties is required to assess individual progress.
Documentation:

Job Title: Landscape & Sustainability Manager
Department: Park Projects & Stewardship
Reports to: Director of Park Projects & Stewardship
Position Status: Full-Time, Exempt
Salary: $70,000 - $80,000
Position Description:
The Esplanade Association is seeking a seasoned Landscape & Sustainability Manager to lead park stewardship, horticultural enhancement, and the long-term ecological sustainability of the Charles River Esplanade. This dynamic management role will be the organization’s eyes and ears throughout the 64-acre Esplanade, tracking and reporting on the condition of living and built infrastructure in the park, and overseeing the day-to-day horticultural, maintenance, and volunteer activities that keep the park thriving, beautiful, well-maintained and environmentally resilient. Working collaboratively with the Esplanade Association’s senior leadership team, the Department of Conservation and Recreation (DCR), staff, volunteers, and partners, this position will guide the strategic vision and implementation of the organization’s landscape, horticulture and sustainability programs. Through thoughtful management, innovation, and effective communication, the Landscape & Sustainability Manager will help ensure that every decision supports the health of the park, enriches the visitor experience, and advances the Esplanade Association’s mission of stewardship and public enjoyment for generations to come.
Job Mission:
Represent the Esplanade Association as the primary resource, both internally and externally, on maintenance and improvement projects on the Charles River Esplanade through innovative living and built infrastructure management, horticultural excellence, environmental initiatives, and community engagement efforts, promoting ecological health, operational resilience, and an exceptional park experience for all.
Key Behaviors:
Strong candidates will:
  • Balance care of the park’s living infrastructure, including trees, lawns, fields, ornamental gardens, and riverbank areas, and its built infrastructure, including benches, seasonal fountains, playgrounds, and bike racks, with a keen eye toward how these features and amenities are affected by regular visitor use, special events, and a changing climate.
  • Apply sustainable land management practices by championing native/near-native and beneficial plantings, water conservation, soil health, and environmentally responsible maintenance techniques.
  • Identify and implement landscape improvements that enhance visitor experience while supporting biodiversity, climate resilience, and environmental stewardship goals.
  • Build strong partnerships with staff, contractors, and stakeholders to successfully plan, maintain, and improve high-quality public landscapes and green infrastructure assets.
Metrics:
The Landscape & Sustainability Manager is successful when:
  • The park’s 1900 trees, 3.3 miles of riverbank, 260+ benches, 13 ornamental gardens, 3 playgrounds, seasonal fountains, and recreational lawns and fields receive planned and ad hoc care in line with DCR and industry standards, on time and on budget.
  • The Park Care team is well managed with clear responsibilities, balanced workloads, and opportunities for professional growth within the organization.
  • EA’s climate action goals are tracked and reported out on a regular basis, and new goals are added in alignment with new research and industry best practices, staff input/ability, and funding availability.
Responsibilities:
Park Stewardship & Horticulture Operations (40%)
  • Lead the planning of annual and seasonal stewardship, maintenance, and enhancement of the Esplanade’s living and built infrastructure, including the Tree Management and Succession Plan [link]
  • Oversee the execution of all landscape and horticultural operations by staff and contractors, including planting design, irrigation, soil health, turf care, nuisance/invasive species control, and tree care.
  • Establish and maintain high standards of horticultural excellence, landscape quality, ecological health, operational efficiency, and visitor experience.
  • Ensure the effective allocation of staff, volunteers, equipment, and resources to support operational goals.
Sustainability & Environmental Operations (20%)
  • Lead the Esplanade Association’s sustainability strategy, advancing initiatives that improve ecological health, climate resilience, and resource conservation in alignment with EA’s 2024 Climate Action Plan [link], environmental regulations, and industry best practices.
  • Oversee environmental projects and research studies, including green infrastructure, stormwater management, riverbank restoration, waste reduction, and energy and water conservation efforts.
  • Track organization-wide sustainability goals and performance metrics and prepare annual reports on progress and impact.
  • Collaborate with staff, partners, and regional organizations to track relevant state and local environmental projects and regulations, advance shared environmental objectives, and promote sustainable practices.
Staff & Contractor Management (20%)
  • Supervise, mentor, and evaluate horticulture staff, seasonal employees, interns, and volunteers.
  • Review current staffing and make recommendations on how to improve workflow processes and assigned responsibilities.
  • Manage contractors and consultants supporting landscape maintenance, tree care, and capital projects.
  • Promote a culture of public approachability and kindness, safety and professionalism, cleanliness and organization, accountability and continuous improvement.
Community Engagement & Partnerships (10%)
  • Build and maintain productive relationships with DCR staff, community partners, donors, volunteers, and stakeholders.
  • Support environmental education, garden tours, public outreach, and sustainability-focused programming.
  • Collaborate with internal teams to integrate landscape and sustainability initiatives into visitor experiences and public programs.
Planning, Administration & Budget Management (10%)
  • Support departmental budgeting, strategic planning, and grant applications and reporting.
  • Maintain presentation-ready inventories, records, GIS/maps, databases, and operational documentation.
  • Manage equipment, tools and vehicles with up-to-date service and maintenance.
Qualifications:
  • Bachelor’s degree in landscape architecture, environmental science, horticulture, sustainability, or related field.
  • 3 to 5 years of project management experience combining grounds/facilities care with environmental strategy.
  • Credentials like SITES AP, ISA Certified Arborist, or MA Master Gardener Certificate help applicants stand out.
  • Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal skills and the ability to build strong professional relationships.
  • Strong project management, organizational, communication, and stakeholder engagement skills to support collaboration with staff, contractors, volunteers, partners, and the public.
  • Experience developing and managing budgets.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite and ability to learn and adapt to various software.
  • Demonstrated ability (or clearly demonstrated capacity) to effectively organize, manage, and motivate staff and volunteers, and ability to work well under pressure or with rapidly changing priorities.
  • Knowledge of the Charles River Esplanade and passion for parks, historic landmarks, recreation, culture, education, green space, and sustainability.
  • Ability to safely operate and/or drive a variety of light and heavy equipment (i.e. chainsaw, pole saw, string trimmer, basic lawnmower, various hand tools, etc.).
  • Must possess a valid Massachusetts driver’s license at time of appointment and for duration of employment.
  • Bilingual or multilingual skills a plus.
Logistics:
  • Work hours are on average 40 hours per week, currently Monday through Friday 9a-5pm with infrequent, predetermined evening and/or weekend commitments. When the Smith Family Pavilion and Charlesbank Campus opens, work hours will be on average 40 hours per week Tuesday to Saturday 9a to 5p. Work hours might vary based on program needs. Prepare for significant variance around the exciting time period of the grand opening, which may require changes for additional evening, weekend, or even early morning hours.
  • Work will require being in both indoor and outdoor settings across seasons.
  • Work will require applicant to bend, reach, carry, climb, and lift 40 lbs. as necessary to perform assigned duties.
  • Applicants are subject to Criminal Offender Record Information (C.O.R.I) check, however, we believe in rehabilitation and will provide any applicant the opportunity to address past work and life experiences.
Compensation:
  • EA offers a competitive salary within the Boston nonprofit and parks sector. The annual salary range for this position is $70,000–$80,000, based on experience, qualifications, and demonstrated skills. This range reflects the maximum compensation available for the role and is not a guarantee of a specific starting salary. EA regularly reviews performance and compensation and provides employees with transparent opportunities for professional growth and advancement.
Benefits:
  • 15 vacation, 12 sick & 2 personal days per year (after 2 years of service, vacation days increase to 17)
  • 11 holidays: Thanksgiving, Christmas, New Years Day, MLK Day, and Presidents Day off, and the 6 remaining as floating holidays depending on holiday worked: Memorial Day, Juneteenth, July 4, Labor Day, Indigenous Peoples Day and Veterans Day.
  • Health and dental insurance, 80% of monthly premium paid by EA
  • Health savings account with $2,500 EA contribution for those enrolled in EA health plan
  • 403(b) retirement plan
  • Commuter benefits, pre-tax deduction up to $300/month
  • Paid professional development opportunities
Application Process:
  • Include 1-page cover letter that addresses this topic: If given the opportunity to improve one aspect of the Esplanade's landscape during your first year, what would you prioritize and why?
  • Resume should include at least 2 references for roles within the past 3 years.
  • Each file name should include the applicant's last name.
The Esplanade Association is an Equal Opportunity Employer and greatly encourages candidates of all backgrounds to apply. Diversity of opinions, experiences, and backgrounds is a key and valued component of our work to promote a welcoming, accessible, and inclusive experience on the Esplanade through an organization that is itself diverse and inclusive.
Not sure you meet 100% of our qualifications? Research shows that men apply for jobs when they meet an average of 60% of the criteria. Yet, women and other people who are systematically marginalized tend to only apply if they meet every requirement. If you believe that you could excel in this role, we encourage you to apply. We are dedicated to considering a broad array of candidates, including those with diverse workplace experiences and backgrounds. Whether you’re new to non-profit administration, returning to work after a gap in employment, simply looking to transition, or take the next step in your career path, we will be glad to have you on our radar. Please use your cover letter to tell us about your interest and what you hope to bring to this role.

title: Designer Integration Engineer
description:
At Mott MacDonald, we are driven by purpose and powered by brilliant people. As a trusted engineering, management, and development consultancy, we work with clients to solve complex challenges and deliver sustainable outcomes that make a meaningful difference for the communities we serve.

When you join us as an experienced professional, you will bring your expertise to work that matters while continuing to grow your career. You will collaborate with talented colleagues across disciplines and geographies, contribute your perspective, and help shape better outcomes through technical excellence, innovation, and integrity.


At Mott MacDonald, we are committed to delivering exceptional outcomes through innovation, collaboration, and technical excellence. As part of a Joint Venture team supporting a large Transportation Authority, we are seeking a Design Integration Engineer - Underground Stations to help deliver one of the largest and most significant transit infrastructure projects in the United States.

This role offers an exciting opportunity to work within a multidisciplinary team on a complex underground transit program, coordinating design interfaces across multiple engineering disciplines to support successful project delivery.

The opportunity

As a Design Integration Engineer, you will support the development and implementation of design integration activities across underground station design packages. Reporting to the Design Integration Manager, you will play a key role in facilitating coordination between engineering disciplines, managing interfaces, and supporting the delivery of integrated design solutions.

Key responsibilities:

  • Support the development and implementation of design and systems integration processes across project design activities.
  • Coordinate multidisciplinary engineering teams, including MEP, systems, civil, and structural disciplines for underground station design.
  • Lead design coordination meetings and facilitate the resolution of complex technical interfaces.
  • Support the Design Integration Manager and Station Design Lead with day-to-day design integration and coordination activities.
  • Coordinate the development and use of 2D and 3D BIM models to support design reviews, clash detection, and issue resolution.
  • Support management of internal, external, third-party, inter-contract, and intra-contract interfaces.
  • Assist with the development and maintenance of Interface Control Documents (ICDs) and interface registers.
  • Evaluate and provide recommendations to support interface and integration decisions while considering broader program objectives and project requirements.
  • Foster collaboration across teams to promote effective communication, risk mitigation, and successful project delivery.

We are looking for a collaborative and proactive professional who enjoys solving complex technical challenges and working within a fast-paced project environment.

Candidate Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering or a related discipline.
  • 5+ years of relevant experience in MEP, systems engineering, communications systems, systems integration, or a related field.
  • Experience supporting multidisciplinary design integration on large-scale infrastructure or rail transit projects.
  • Proficiency with Revit and BIM-based coordination processes.
  • Strong understanding of multidisciplinary design coordination and interface management.
  • Excellent communication, organizational, and analytical skills.
  • Ability to build effective relationships across diverse project teams and stakeholders.
  • Authorization to work in the United States without sponsorship.

Preferred experience

  • Experience on major rail, transit, transportation, or tunnel projects.
  • Familiarity with complex underground station design and delivery.
  • Experience developing Interface Control Documents and managing technical interfaces throughout the design lifecycle.
  • Knowledge of BIM coordination and clash detection workflows.

Build on your experience while helping shape what comes next. At Mott MacDonald, you'll work alongside talented people on complex and rewarding projects that make a real difference. We value fresh perspectives, encourage collaboration, and provide opportunities to expand your skills, take on new challenges, and grow your career. Whether you're deepening your technical expertise, broadening your leadership experience, or exploring new opportunities across our business, you'll be supported by a team that is committed to helping you succeed.

This position is located in San Jose, CA. You must be able to reliably commute to our office in this location, per our hybrid working policy.

Bring your expertise, curiosity, and drive to make a difference. If you are ready to join a collaborative consultancy where your perspective is valued, your growth is supported, and you are empowered to lead with integrity, we would love to hear from you.

Benefits & Rewards

The expected salary for this position is $96,000 - $118,000.

Individual pay is determined based on several factors such as work location, education, experience, and unique skills.

In addition to base salary, Mott MacDonald offers performance-based bonuses and a comprehensive benefits package, giving employees a direct connection to our success.

Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to support the health, wellbeing, financial security, and professional growth of our employees. Eligible employees have access to medical, dental, and vision coverage, FSA and HSA accounts, company-paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability coverage, and a competitive 401(k) plan with company matching. We also provide paid time off, paid holidays, caregiver leave, employee referral bonuses, professional registration and membership reimbursements, and tuition assistance to support continued learning and career development.

Collaboration at Our Core

At Mott MacDonald, we believe great ideas happen when we're together. Our hybrid approach centers on an in-office culture, with most of your time spent collaborating face-to-face and a minimum of three days per week in the office. We balance flexibility with connection, so you and your manager can choose how to meet clients, team, and personal commitments.

Equal opportunity is the law.

We seek to promote fair employment procedures and practices to ensure equal opportunities for all. We encourage individual expression in our workplace and are committed to creating an inclusive environment where everyone feels they have the opportunity to contribute.

title: Driving Instructor - CO
description:
CLICK THE CITY & STATE ABOVE TO VIEW OUR EXACT LOCATION


About us

Coastline Academy is the largest and fastest growing driving school in the country. Since 2017 we've taught more than 250,000 students across seven states, backed by over 100,000 five-star reviews. We're on a mission to eradicate car crashes by teaching safe and confident drivers for life. We're people-first and technology-centric: online booking, digital lesson reports, transparent pricing, modern cars. 98% of our students rate their lesson five stars.

Become part of a team committed to creating safe, confident drivers for life.


About this role

You'll sit in the passenger seat of a Coastline car and teach people something they'll use every day for the rest of their lives. Most of your students are teenagers taking their first turn behind the wheel. Some are adults getting ready for a road test. All of them leave your car more capable than when they got in.

  • You teach in our car, not yours. Every Coastline vehicle is company-provided, clearly marked, fitted with a second instructor brake, and inspected by certified mechanics.
  • We pay for your certification. Our training team walks you through your state's driving instructor licensing requirements and provides the coursework. Training is paid.
  • Every lesson is recorded. Dashcams capture video and audio inside and outside the car for your safety and your student's.
  • Your schedule follows the students. Most of our students are in school, so demand concentrates in afternoons and weekends. A typical day is three two-hour lessons.


What does training entail?


Training Breakdown (30 Hours Total):

  • 15 Hours Virtual Learning: Self-paced home reading and module completion.
  • 12 Hours Hands-On Driving & Practical Mentorship: Shadow 6 hours live in-car lessons (three 2-hour lessons with student) and complete 6 hours of direct coaching with a Certified Trainer (two 3-hour sessions).
  • 3 Hours Administrative Tasks: Essential training on policy, reporting, and operational procedures.


What you'll do

  • Teach the practical skills of driving, every aspect, from parking lots to freeway merges
  • Coach students on the rules of the road
  • Build confidence, not just competence
  • Take control of the vehicle when a situation calls for it
  • Document and report on each student's progress
  • Stay in close, timely communication with your supervisor and support team
  • Bring professionalism to every interaction with students and teammates
  • Show up for team meetings, updates, and ongoing development

title: Automotive Lube Tech
description:
We're growing and we'd love to have you grow with us

Atlantic Coast Enterprises is seeking to hire part-time and full-time Automotive Technicians to provide top-notch service at a Jiffy Lube in Tampa, FL. Are you looking to learn and advance your skills with a company that cares about its employees? Do you want to work in a collaborative, positive environment where humor, teamwork, and laughter are encouraged? If so, keep reading!

Our Automotive Technicians/Auto Mechanics earn a salary of up to $40,000 per year based on experience. We also offer generous benefits including paid vacation after one year of employment, longevity bonuses, comprehensive health care, dental/vision insurance, basic life insurance, short-term disability, long-term disability, a 401(k) plan, bereavement leave, and employee oil changes and discounts. If this sounds like the right part-time or full-time position for you, apply today!

ABOUT ATLANTIC COAST ENTERPRISES

Atlantic Coast Enterprises (ACE) is a full-service lubrication, fluid, and automotive maintenance center. We offer our customers these services in the cleanest, most professional surroundings possible. Each day we strive to achieve our mission to create customers for life through fast, friendly, clean, and professional service. We are dedicated to expanding and moving constantly on to new and different challenges. A few short years ago, we were recognized as the franchisee of the year within the Jiffy Lube nationwide network.

Everything at ACE is a team effort. We know that without our employees we wouldn't be able to grow, improve, or create lifelong customers. This is why we offer competitive compensation, generous benefits, and a supportive, collaborative environment. We encourage each and every employee to share their ideas with us.

A DAY IN THE LIFE OF A LUBE TECH

You arrive each day determined to take excellent care of our customers. They trust your competence, as well as your integrity to keep their vehicles running. Utilizing the training we have provided, you are able to correctly identify mechanical problems, provide preventative maintenance, and carefully address customer concerns. With your excellent communication skills, you give recommendations for repairs along with proper labor and time estimates. You then make the repairs and replace parts as requested. Your positive attitude and ability to stay on top of the latest knowledge and training ensure your success!

QUALIFICATIONS

  • At least 18 years old
  • Valid driver's license
  • Physical ability to perform typical tasks required for repairing and servicing vehicles including the ability to stand for several hours at a time and lift up to 50 lbs
  • Comfortable working in a variety of weather conditions

No experience? Don't worry! We will teach you everything you need to know. Any previous experience is a plus! Do you have excellent mechanical skills and the drive to problem-solve? Are you able to work independently and in a team environment? Do you have exceptional customer service skills? If so, you may be perfect for this part-time or full-time position!

WORK SCHEDULE

Our Lube Techs work anywhere from 15-40 hours/week depending on part-time or full-time status. The typical work schedule varies during our business hours and will include a mix of day, evening, and weekend shifts--but no late nights. We are open 8am to 7pm Monday-Saturday and 9am to 4pm on Sunday.

ARE YOU READY TO JOIN OUR TEAM?

If you feel that you are right for this position, apply now with our initial 3-minute, mobile-friendly application.

Job Title: Programs Manager
Department: Visitor Services
Reports to: Director of Visitor Services
Position Status: Full-Time, Exempt
Salary: $70,000 - $80,000
Position Description:
The Esplanade Association seeks a seasoned Programs Manager to broaden the programming on the Charles River Esplanade and at our soon-to-be opened Charlesbank Campus and Smith Family Pavilion. Reporting to the Director of Visitor Services, the Programs Manager will play a key role in shaping the visitor experience through the development, coordination, and execution of year-round programming. This position is responsible for creating and managing a diverse portfolio of recreational, cultural, educational, and community-based programs that activate the campus and advance the Esplanade Association's mission of welcoming all visitors.
The Programs Manager will lead the planning and delivery of various programs including stage performances, concerts, court-based leagues and tournaments, wellness and recreational programming, and community events. Working closely with internal and external partners, the Programs Manager will build relationships with performers, instructors, athletic organizations, cultural institutions, sponsors, and community groups to maximize visitor engagement through many modes. As the Charlesbank Campus debuts and expands programming opportunities, the Programs Manager will maximize those opportunities by overseeing program logistics, scheduling, vendor coordination, contract administration, and RFP development related to programming. The position will collaborate closely with other staff to ensure exceptional visitor experiences and seamless campus operations.
Job Mission:
The Programs Manager, along with the rest of the Visitor Services team, will create diverse, high-quality programming that serves local residents, visitors from far and near, and partner organizations.They will contribute significantly to the transformation of – and subsequently maintenance and growth of – the Charlesbank Pavilion Campus into a year-round destinationfor live entertainment, athletics, education, and community connection.
Key Behaviors:
Strong candidates will:
  • Create welcoming, inclusive experiences rooted in hospitality, accessibility, and fun.
  • Communicate well in person and in writing.
  • Build strong relationships with staff, partners, vendors, performers, volunteers, and visitors.
  • Use sound judgment and adapt in a fast-paced public setting.
  • Develop creative partnerships and programs that strengthen audience engagement and the visitor experience.
  • Manage programs, budgets, data, schedules, contracts, and reporting with accuracy.
  • Embody a warm, energetic, and outgoing attitude.
Metrics:
The Programs Manager is successful when:
  • Programs meet or exceed attendance and engagement goals.
  • Visitors, participants, and partners report highly positive and recommendable experiences.
  • Campus utilization grows through diverse performances, tournaments, educational offerings, and community programs.
  • Programs are delivered efficiently through strong staff, vendor, and partner collaboration.
  • You can regularly practice agility in program design and timelines, from year-long concert planning to spur-of-the-moment pop-up experimentation
About the Esplanade Association (www.esplanade.org):
Founded in 2001, the Esplanade Association (EA) is the community-supported non-profit dedicated to expanding the care of and for the historic Charles River Esplanade through projects, programs and plantings that amplify the park experience for over 4 million visitors annually. The Esplanade is downtown Boston’s 64-acre state park maintained by the Massachusetts Department of Conservation and Recreation (DCR). This cultural landmark is revered for its natural and cultivated beauty, history, riverfront access, miles of popular running and biking trails, and dynamic programs with numerous organizations. EA’s contributions include funding and implementing the following enhancements, revitalizations and activations: over 150 service, educational, recreational and cultural programs offered annually; over 300 new trees planted through the Lasting Esplanade Arbor Fund (L.E.A.F.); repair or reconstruction of beloved amenities including Lotta Fountain, Community Boating docks and Centennial Fountain; both temporary and long-term public art commissions; playground maintenance and accessible design, including the Gronk Playground in 2025; construction underway to open in 2026 the Esplanade’s new Smith Family Pavilion and Charlesbank Campus, improving two-acres to equitably welcome more people from more places to a year-round destination in the park; and much more. It's an exciting time to join our community-engaged non-profit as it grows in scale, visibility, and impact.
Responsibilities:
Program Operations (70%)
  • Develop and manage a robust annual slate of programs and activities across the Charles River Esplanade, with an emphasis on the new Charlesbank Campus.
  • Coordinate performances, concerts, festivals, theatrical productions, and community events utilizing indoor and outdoor spaces.
  • Determine and respond to audience interest and capacity for different styles and types of programs
  • Identify opportunities to attract innovative performers, cultural organizations, and entertainment partners.
  • Oversee program logistics including scheduling, set up and breakdown, staffing, permits, equipment, registration, adherence to safety requirements, and vendor coordination.
  • Lead the development, issuance, and evaluation of Requests for Proposals (RFPs) related to programming, entertainment, event production, concessions, facility services, and vendor partnerships.
  • Serve as liaison between performers, promoters, and production teams with campus stakeholders.
  • Coordinate program site layouts, sharing proposed site plans and coordinating with operations staff to communicate the impact of programs on the park.
  • Coordinate technical requirements including sound, lighting, staging, and production support.
  • Develop best practices for use of programmable spaces on the Charlesbank Campus.
  • In collaboration with Programs team and other staff, manage programs supply of equipment, coordination of pick-up, and storage
  • Monitor vendor performance and ensure contractual obligations are met.
  • Evaluate program success through attendance, participant feedback, and revenue goals.
  • Reflect regularly on program strengths and weaknesses, and offer creative ideas to enhance the portfolio
Business Development & Partnerships (10%)
  • Cultivate, maintain, and document relationships with sponsors, community organizations, arts groups, educational institutions, and program producers.
  • Contribute to the production of annual partnership convenings hosted by EA.
  • Secure partnerships that increase campus visibility, participation, and revenue generation.
  • Identify new programming opportunities that align with campus goals and community interests.
  • Assist with sponsorship packages, funding opportunities, and periodic Development initiatives and events.
Marketing & Outreach (10%)
  • Develop and manage program registration webpages.
  • Work closely with marketing staff to develop compelling online and printed marketing materials to drive participation in EA programs, particularly with a focus on broadening EA’s audience.
  • Manage pre- and post-program communications to registrants including but not limited to program info, follow-up surveys, cancellations/postponements, reminders, and updates.
  • Work closely with marketing staff to ensure EA activities are shared with wide-reaching media outlets and calendar listing services, including those sharing program information in languages other than English.
  • Participate in periodic community and networking events on behalf of EA to build awareness of our programs.
  • Actively support superior visitor experience in all aspects of work including frequent conversations, wayfinding help, and inquiry response in the park and at the Charlesbank Campus info desk.
  • Provide auxiliary support for volunteer programs and strengthen volunteer relationships with EA.
Budget & Administration (10%)
  • Contribute to annual departmental budget plan
  • Develop and execute assigned programs portfolio within allocated budget including monitoring expenses, revenues, and financial performance
  • Coordinate RFP vendor selection processes and contract administration.
  • Assist in the preparation of reports, programming recommendations, and performance metrics for leadership.
  • Support hiring process and oversight of seasonal Programs staff.
  • Ensure compliance with organizational policies, safety requirements, and applicable regulations.
Qualifications:
  • Bachelor’s degree in Event Management, Recreation Management, Arts Administration, or related field.
  • 3–5 years of experience in events, community programming, venue operations, stage management, or public-facing programs.
  • Experience coordinating performances, athletic events, educational programs, or public events.
  • Strong collaboration skills with staff, vendors, volunteers, partners, and the public.
  • Commitment to a positive visitor experience.
  • A demonstrated history of cultural competence.
  • Strong project management, organizational, communication, and stakeholder engagement skills.
  • Experience developing and managing budgets.
  • Knowledge of event production, stage operations, sound, lighting, RFPs, procurement, sponsorships, and partnerships preferred.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite.
  • Relevant networks of vendors, clients, partners, or attendees a plus.
  • Knowledge of the Charles River Esplanade and passion for parks, historic landmarks, recreation, culture, education, green space, and sustainability a plus.
  • Bilingual or multilingual skills a plus.
Logistics:
  • Work hours are on average 40 hours per week, currently Monday through Friday 9a-5pm with infrequent, predetermined weekend commitments. When the Esplanade Smith Family Pavilion and Charlesbank Campus opens, work hours will be on average 40 hours per week Tuesday to Saturday 11a to 7p. Work hours might vary based on program needs. Prepare for significant variance around the exciting time period of the grand opening, which may require changes for additional evening, weekend, or even early morning hours.
  • Must be available to work a flexible schedule related to events on nights, weekends and some holidays.
  • Work will require being in both indoor and outdoor settings across seasons.
  • Work will require applicant to bend, reach, carry, climb, and lift 40 lbs. as necessary to perform assigned duties.
  • Applicants are subject to Criminal Offender Record Information (C.O.R.I) check, however, we believe in rehabilitation and will provide any applicant the opportunity to address past work and life experiences.
Compensation:
  • EA offers a competitive salary within the Boston nonprofit and parks sector. The annual salary range for this position is $70,000–$80,000, based on experience, qualifications, and demonstrated skills. This range reflects the maximum compensation available for the role and is not a guarantee of a specific starting salary. EA regularly reviews performance and compensation and provides employees with transparent opportunities for professional growth and advancement.
Benefits:
  • 15 vacation, 12 sick & 2 personal days per year (after 2 years of service, vacation days increase to 17)
  • 11 holidays, Thanksgiving, Christmas, New Years Day, MLK Day, and Presidents Day off and the 6 remaining as floating holidays depending on holiday worked, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, July 4, Labor Day, Indigenous Peoples Day and Veterans Day.
  • Health and dental insurance, 80% of monthly premium paid by EA
  • Health savings account with $2,500 EA contribution for those enrolled in EA health plan
  • 403(b) retirement plan
  • Commuter benefits, pre-tax deduction up to $300/month
  • Paid professional development opportunities
Application Process:
  • Include 1-page cover letter that addresses this topic: Refer to your prior experience and tell us about a memorable event or program you have hosted. Who was the audience? Summarize the preparations you made for the occasion. What do you think made the event resonate with participants?
  • Resume should include at least 2 references for roles within the past 3 years.
  • Each file name should include the applicant's last name.

title: Network Order Preparation and Projects Specialist
description:
At The One 23 Group, our mission is to set the benchmark for excellence in government services. We empower our clients in the Department of Defense, Intelligence Community, and Federal Civilian sectors to excel with our advanced capabilities. Our dedication lies in fostering a people-first culture, underpinned by steadfast ethical principles. Embracing innovative technologies and process improvements, we are steadfast in our journey toward a future that is both bright and transformative.


Our expertise spans Enterprise IT, Mission IT and Cyber. With our global footprint, we place a strong emphasis on nurturing our people and culture, which forms the core of our successful strategies in leadership and financial management. We pride ourselves on our extensive experience and effective approach, ensuring that we lead with both innovation and integrity.


THE POSITION

Serve as a customer service–oriented Network Special Projects and Order Preparation Specialist for the DISN Consolidated Provisioning (DCP) effort. This role supports the full provisioning lifecycle—order entry, preparation, solution design, and circuit activation—while coordinating end-to-end delivery of network requirements. The position holds overall “Service Delivery” accountability, ensuring system efficiency, accurate circuit documentation, and cost-effective provisioning using DISN or commercial resources.


RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Provide advanced network infrastructure and administrative support for DISA systems to meet mission objectives.
  • Develop, transition, and document service orders; maintain accurate circuit and system records.
  • Manage enterprise-wide networks (CAN, MAN, WAN) across classified/unclassified environments and resolve escalations.
  • Perform systems analysis, prepare deliverables, and support architecture compliance with DISA and OSI/ISO standards.
  • Ensure Telecommunications Service Priority (TSP) compliance and validate QoS metrics for DISN and commercial trunks.
  • Configure, optimize, and document network servers, components, and circuit paths for high performance.
  • Lead cross-functional teams, provide technical guidance, and implement sustainable solutions through root cause analysis.
  • Support large-scale provisioning (~1,000 leased circuits annually and ~1,500 draft service orders monthly).
  • Oversee upgrades, installations, maintenance, and EIS transition activities, including TSIPs and project updates.
  • Deliver specialized projects (emergency provisioning, pilot programs, multi-site connectivity, and security enhancements).


ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

  • On-site in Columbus, OH.
  • Day shift with flexibility to work an alternate or swing shift, as business needs dictate.

  • 3 years or more experience in Human Resources in hotel or related industry

title: Dialysis Tech TTS and MWF - Full Time/Per diem
description:
Job Summary:

Under the supervision and/or direction of the Chief Technician, Nurse Manager, Charge Nurse or Staff RN, may perform various duties assisting nursing staff in the preparation of dialysis equipment and in the treatment and care of patients, in accordance to established policies and procedures of the Center.

Qualifications:

1. High School graduate.
2. American Heart Association, BLS Provider Card - Required
3. Hemodialysis Certification through either the Board of Nephrolou Examiners Nursing and Technology (BONENT) or through the National Association of Nephrology Technicians/ Technologist (NANT). - Required
4. Able to read and speak English - bilingual preferred
5. One year experience in the medical field either as a certified hemodialysis technician involved in patient care - preferred

Duties and Responsibilities:

Patient Care Activities:

l . Perform routine treatment procedures such as insertion of fistula needles, initiation, and termination of treatments.

2. Administration of Heparin and Normal Saline, as required and ordered.

3. Perform pre-dialysis safety tests and document properly.

4. Check, adjust and record blood flow rate, machine pressures, Heparin dosage/administration when taking blood pressure during treatment procedure.

5. Make rounds to assigned patients, anticipate needs, answer patients' calls, and respond to visual and audible alarms of equipment.

6. Ensure all safety parameters on the equipment are set and maintained.

7. Assist in the positioning, lifting, and turning of patients using proper body mechanics.
Take vital signs before, during and after dialysis procedure to assigned patients.

8. Monitor patients during dialysis procedure. Report any unusual changes, signs or symptoms to the nurse.
9. Obtain blood specimen as ordered and required. Label blood properly and complete requisitions.
1 0. Spin blood specimens in the Centrifuge, as required and directed.
1 1 . Complete appropriate documentation after each task. Report unusual events to the immediate supervisor.

Other Activities:

1. Perform Hard Water test, as assigned.
2. Perform Chloramine tests, as assigned.
3. Keep various logs updated, per policy.
4. Prepare, gather, distribute supplies prior to treatment or as per established routine procedures.
5. Re-stock supplies in designated areas.
6. Receive and store shipments of supplies. Verify amount and type of supplies received. Submit packing slips immediately to appropriate personnel.
7. Clean and maintain dialysis and accessory equipment per policy.
8. Assist in maintaining a safe and clean environment by reporting equipment that is out of order and other problems to the supervisor.
9. Establish and maintain good interpersonal relationships with patients, visitors, and unit personnel, while maintaining confidentiality of patient information.
10, Participate in and contribute to staff meetings and other unit activities.
11. Attend in-service education programs as directed, to learn new treatment skills, procedures, etc.

title: Software Engineering Intern
description:
Software Engineering Intern
Location: Lafayette, LA (Preferred)
Type: Internship (Part-Time or Full-Time Available)
About DMR Technologies
DMR Technologies is a Louisiana-based drone manufacturer developing industry-leading solutions for agriculture, public safety, critical infrastructure, and defense. As a fast-growing technology company, we build much more than drones—we create the software, automation, and internal systems that power every part of our business.
We're looking for a Software Engineering Intern who enjoys building things, learning quickly, and leveraging modern AI development tools to solve real-world business problems.
What You'll Do
As a Software Engineering Intern, you'll work directly with company leadership to design and develop internal software that improves efficiency across the organization. Projects move quickly, and your work will be used by real employees and customers.
Projects may include:
  • Building features for DMR's custom internal ERP platform
  • Developing web applications using JavaScript and React
  • Creating internal business tools and workflow automation
  • Assisting with website development and content updates
  • Developing customer-facing and internal web applications
  • Building and configuring AI-powered agents and chatbots using platforms such as Open Claw
  • Integrating APIs and third-party software
  • Assisting with light UI/UX improvements and basic graphic design
  • Troubleshooting, testing, and improving existing software solutions
No two weeks are exactly alike, and interns are encouraged to contribute ideas and own projects from concept through deployment.
Preferred Qualifications
  • Currently pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field
  • Experience with JavaScript
  • Familiarity with React
  • Basic understanding of HTML and CSS
  • Comfortable using Git or other version control systems
  • Strong problem-solving skills
  • Self-motivated and eager to learn new technologies
Bonus Experience
Experience with any of the following is a plus:
  • TypeScript
  • Node.js
  • REST APIs
  • SQL databases
  • Python
  • Mobile app development
  • UI/UX design
  • WordPress or website management
  • AI-assisted development tools such as Claude, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, or similar
  • Prompt engineering and AI workflow automation
What We're Looking For
We care less about checking every technical box and more about finding someone who loves building software.
The ideal candidate:
  • Enjoys figuring things out independently
  • Learns new technologies quickly
  • Isn't afraid to experiment
  • Can turn ideas into working software
  • Uses AI tools effectively while still understanding the code they're writing
  • Communicates well with both technical and non-technical teammates
Why DMR?
As an intern, you won't spend your summer fixing minor bugs or working on isolated assignments. You'll build software that is actively used throughout the company and have direct exposure to executive leadership, product development, manufacturing, sales, and operations.
You'll gain hands-on experience with:
  • Modern JavaScript development
  • React applications
  • AI-assisted software development
  • Business software architecture
  • Rapid product development
  • Startup technology culture
  • Real-world problem solving
If you're excited about building software, experimenting with AI, and seeing your work make an immediate impact, we'd love to meet you.

title: Drone Systems Engineering  Intern
description:
Drone Systems Engineering Intern

Location: Lafayette, LA (Preferred)
Type: Internship (Part-Time or Full-Time)

About DMR Technologies

DMR Technologies designs and manufactures advanced unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) serving agriculture, public safety, critical infrastructure, and defense. Our products combine mechanical engineering, electronics, embedded systems, software, manufacturing, and autonomous flight into complete solutions built in Louisiana. We’re seeking a Drone Systems Engineering Intern who enjoys building things, solving problems, and learning across multiple engineering disciplines.

What You'll Do

As a Drone Systems Engineering Intern, you'll gain hands-on experience supporting the design, assembly, testing, and deployment of next-generation unmanned aircraft systems.

Projects may include:

  • Assisting with the design and development of drone platforms
  • Building and testing prototype aircraft
  • Supporting mechanical, electrical, and software integration
  • Assisting with flight testing and data collection
  • Troubleshooting hardware and system-level issues
  • Supporting manufacturing process improvements
  • Assisting with CAD models, engineering documentation, and BOM updates
  • Integrating sensors, payloads, cameras, communications equipment, and accessories
  • Supporting internal software tools, automation, or AI-powered engineering workflows
  • Working alongside engineering, production, and flight operations teams
No two weeks are the same. Interns are encouraged to contribute ideas, solve problems, and take ownership of meaningful projects.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Pursuing a degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Computer Engineering, Robotics, Computer Science, or a related technical field
  • Strong mechanical aptitude
  • Excellent problem-solving skills
  • Comfortable working with tools and hands-on equipment
  • Curious, self-motivated, and eager to learn
Bonus Experience

Experience with any of the following is a plus:

  • CAD (SolidWorks, Fusion 360, or similar)
  • Electronics and soldering
  • Embedded systems or microcontrollers
  • JavaScript, Python, or C++
  • React or web application development
  • AI-assisted development tools (Claude, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, etc.)
  • Robotics or autonomous systems
  • 3D printing
  • Drone building or FPV experience
  • FAA Part 107 Remote Pilot Certificate
What We're Looking For

We care less about checking every box and more about finding builders. The ideal candidate enjoys taking things apart, figuring out how they work, improving them, and building something even better.

Why DMR?

You'll work directly with engineers, technicians, manufacturing, software developers, and company leadership while contributing to products that are deployed in the real world—not hypothetical classroom projects. You’ll leave with experience spanning engineering, manufacturing, software, testing, and product development that few internships can offer.

title: Oncologist/Hematologist
description:
Novellis Health is a thriving, independently physician-owned and managed private practice—join our stable, growing team focused on personalized, compassionate patient care.

Summary
We are seeking a skilled and compassionate board-certified medical oncologist and hematologist to join our growing team. The successful candidate will deliver high-quality clinical care in both our Richmond Hill and Brooklyn locations, collaborating with a seasoned multidisciplinary team.

Responsibilities
  • Evaluate, diagnose, and treat patients with oncologic and hematologic disorders.
  • Develop individualized treatment plans in consultation with patients and care teams.
  • Administer and oversee chemotherapy, immunotherapy, targeted therapy, and other specialized treatments.
  • Interpret diagnostic tests, including laboratory, imaging, and pathology results.
  • Educate patients and families regarding diagnoses, prognosis, and treatment options.
  • Actively participate in multidisciplinary case discussions and tumor boards.
  • Collaborate with other specialists, nurses, and support staff to coordinate comprehensive care.
  • Participate in research, quality improvement, and educational initiatives as appropriate.
  • Maintain accurate and timely documentation in the electronic health record.
  • Ensure compliance with all federal, state, and institutional regulations.
Qualifications
  • Medical Doctor (MD) or Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine (DO) degree.
  • Board Certification in Medical Oncology and Hematology.
  • Active and unrestricted NY State Medical License (or eligibility).
  • Completion of an accredited fellowship in Medical Oncology & Hematology.
  • Proven track record of clinical excellence in outpatient and inpatient settings.
  • Excellent communication, interpersonal, and organizational skills.
  • Demonstrated commitment to continuing education and evidence-based practice.
  • Additional languages highly preferred, especially Haitian Creole.
Benefits
  • Highly competitive base salary and comprehensive benefits package.
  • Supportive, collaborative, and mission-driven work culture.
  • Access to advanced diagnostic and therapeutic technology.

Motivated to succeed, you build a winning team by recruiting, training, and directing employees so that we can provide exceptional customer service. Each day, you are ready to "roll up your sleeves" and get to work to ensure the success of our vehicle service centers/auto stores.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • 3+ years of extraordinary management experience
  • Valid state driver's license with a clean driving record and access to reliable transportation

Have you built an established reputation as a top performer? Do you have unwavering integrity? Are you a strong leader who can motivate others? Job Title: Exercise, Fitness and Health Coach at The Exercise Coach
Pay Rate: $17-$20/hour. We have openings in our Libertyville and Park Ridge, IL studios.
At The Exercise Coach we are passionate about delivering effective and efficient, science-based Personal Training. We are not a gym. We specialize in one-on-one and semi-private personal training, by appointment only, in a small, clean, and private setting.

Our passion is to inspire and empower people to overcome the six most common excuses for not exercising regularly:

· I don’t have time.
· I don’t know what to do when I go to a gym.
· I don’t like big, crowded gyms, where I have to wait in line to use equipment.
· I am afraid of getting hurt.
· I am in such bad shape; I am embarrassed to be seen at a gym.
· I don’t like to exercise (but I know I need to exercise).

We utilize unique, proprietary technology (Exerbotics.com) that gives our Clients instant feedback during each session, and the ability to track their progress over time with an app for their phone.

Our program enables our Clients to get all the exercise they need in only 20 minutes, twice a week. We know it can be hard to understand how that is possible, which is why we always offer 2 free, no-obligations sessions to allow new prospects the opportunity to experience this efficient method of exercise.

Our #1 priority is Client safety; everything we do is very slow and controlled. And we save our Clients considerable time and money compared to hiring a personal trainer.

Our #1 requirement for Coaching candidates is that they have the ability to engage in conversation very naturally and comfortably with people ages 15 – 90+. Prior fitness experience is not required, but if you have a degree in Kinesiology or Exercise Science, that would be a plus. Our Franchise in-house certification program will give you all the tools you need to be a highly effective Certified Exercise Coach.

We are looking for: 1) Communication skills, enthusiasm, and positive attitude; 2) People skills and personality; 3) Passion for health and fitness.

Successful candidates will complete The Exercise Coach Certification Program, the Nutrition Playbook Certification Program, CPR/AED certification from our preferred provider, and you will shadow experience Coaches until we determine you are ready for final review and Certification. You will be paid for all training hours, and all scheduled hours (not just when coaching Clients). Must be eligible to work in the USA.

The Exercise Coach Franchise has more than 225 studios open in the USA. We were the 1st Franchisees of The Exercise Coach, 15 years ago. We now own and operate studios in Libertyville, Palatine, Arlington Heights, and Park Ridge, IL. We will be adding two new lines of business later this year and expect significant growth and opportunities for our Team.

Who We Are

Established in 1970, Serving Seniors helps San Diego County’s low-income seniors overcome poverty through whole-person, wraparound support including meals, housing, health and social services, and enrichment activities. We work at numerous sites across the county and in the homes of hundreds of homebound seniors. Our flagship Gary & Mary West Senior Wellness Center in downtown San Diego is unlike any other senior center in the nation. Bringing together a range of supportive services under one roof, the Senior Wellness Center operates 365 days a year and offers two floors of integrated care, including health and social services, housing navigation, enrichment activities, lifelong learning, a Cyber Café and linkage to over 25 onsite direct service partners, including a senior dental center. Last fiscal year, we provided over 1.1 million meals and coordinated services to over 14,000 older adults.


Our Mission: Helping seniors in poverty live healthy and fulfilling lives.

Our Vision: All seniors, regardless of income, are able to thrive, engage in their communities, lead purposeful lives, and have a place they call home.

Our Core Values:

Advocacy - Acknowledging and supporting the needs of older adults at the individual, community, and policy-level.

Person-Centered - Seeing the whole person, providing coordinated support, and treating all with dignity and respect.

Integrity – Representing the values of honesty, trust, and transparency within our community.

Compassion & Empathy – Approaching our work with a heartfelt desire to better understand and serve.

Impact – Measuring and evaluating programs to ensure that for every dollar invested, there is a positive impact in the lives of those we serve.

Inclusive – Promoting an environment that nurtures differences and allows individuals to be their entire, authentic selves.

Top Workplace Award Recipient

Serving Seniors has received the San Diego Union-Tribune’s Top Workplaces Award twelve out of the thirteen years the awards program has taken place, and most recently for six years in a row from 2019-2025.

The Activities and Volunteer Coordinator is responsible for implementing and supporting activities at various sites associated with Serving Seniors. Position Overview
Floor Interior Services (FIS) is seeking professional, dependable Measure Technicians to perform accurate in-home flooring measurements and deliver an exceptional customer experience.
This is an independent contractor opportunity. The Measure Technician will visit customers’ homes, evaluate project conditions, accurately measure all applicable areas, document project requirements, upload completed information, and provide the customer with an in-home installation quote.

Key Responsibilities
• Travel to scheduled customer appointments within the assigned service area.
• Contact customers before arrival and maintain professional communication regarding appointment timing.
• Arrive on time, professionally dressed, and prepared to complete the assignment.
• Accurately measure rooms, closets, stairs, transitions, doorways, and other applicable installation areas.
• Identify flooring types, subfloor conditions, transitions, furniture requirements, removal needs, installation challenges, and other project-specific details.
• Create accurate diagrams, room layouts, measurements, photographs, and supporting documentation.
• Ensure all required project information is complete before leaving the customer’s home.
• Upload measurements, diagrams, photographs, notes, and other required documentation within established timelines.
• Review the proposed installation scope with the customer and provide an accurate in-home quote using company-approved systems and pricing.
• Clearly explain the installation process, anticipated requirements, and next steps without making unauthorized promises.
• Answer customer questions professionally and help create confidence in moving forward with the project.
• Immediately report safety concerns, unusual site conditions, system issues, or potential scope problems.
• Protect customer information and maintain confidentiality.
• Correct measurement or documentation errors promptly when responsible for the original assignment.

Performance Expectations
Success in this role will be measured by:
• Measurement accuracy
• Quote accuracy and completeness
• On-time appointment arrival
• Timely data and documentation uploads
• Customer satisfaction
• Quote participation and conversion results
• Professional communication
• Low remeasure and correction rates
• Compliance with FIS and retail-partner requirements
Accuracy is non-negotiable. A rushed or incomplete measurement creates problems for the customer, installer, retailer, and company. Measure twice, upload once—the tape measure has no sympathy.

Required Qualifications
• Experience in flooring measurement, flooring installation, construction, estimating, in-home sales, or a related field is preferred.
• Strong mathematical, measuring, and spatial-reasoning skills.
• Ability to learn and accurately use electronic measuring and quoting systems.
• Comfortable presenting pricing and speaking directly with customers in their homes.
• Strong attention to detail and commitment to completing documentation correctly.
• Professional appearance, communication, and customer-service skills.
• Dependable transportation and willingness to travel throughout the assigned territory.
• Smartphone, tablet, or other required technology capable of running company-approved applications.

title: Clinical Development Associate
location: US Remote - WA, MA, NC, NJ, NH, NM, NY, PA, SC, SD, TX, KY, MS, WI, IN applicants only
description:
JOB TITLE: Clinical Development Associate

LOCATION: Remote (WA or MA preferred) - candidates based in the following states will be considered: IN, MA, NC, NJ, NH, NM, NY, PA, SC, SD, TX, KY, WI, MS or WA.

REPORTS TO: Director, Clinical Science

SALARY RANGE: $92,000 to $120,000


ABOUT THE POSITION

Aurion Biotech is a clinical-stage biotechnology company dedicated to restoring vision to millions of patients through innovative regenerative therapies. Our lead candidate is an allogeneic cell therapy designed to treat corneal edema secondary to corneal endothelial disease. Our cell therapy is PMDA approved, and commercialization started in Japan in 2024. In the US, the program has received both Breakthrough Therapy and Regenerative Medicine Advanced Therapy designations from the FDA and has advanced into Phase 3 clinical trials in 2026. Aurion operates as a separate entity with full support from Alcon.


The Clinical Development Associate will support the clinical development team with day-to-day clinical trial execution, including data and safety review, safety and efficacy metric tracking, and internal and external cross-functional collaboration to help advance Aurion Biotech’s clinical programs.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Support the clinical development team with ongoing scientific and medical oversight and support throughout study startup, enrollment, conduct, database lock, and study closeout
  • Support Medical Monitoring activities and contribute to patient cleaning activities, including assisting with medical monitor query management
  • Identify clinical risks and proactively help develop mitigation strategies
  • Support the clinical scientist with development of study protocols, protocol amendments, informed consent documents, case report forms, and other clinical study documents
  • Collaborate with the clinical scientist to help address protocol questions, eligibility determinations, deviations, and study conduct challenges
  • Ensure clinical studies are conducted in accordance with protocol requirements, ICH-GCP, applicable regulations, and Aurion SOPs
  • Partner with Biometrics and/or Data Management to help develop data review plans and ensure data quality
  • Support ongoing review of clinical, efficacy, safety, imaging, and biomarker/pharmacokinetic data
  • Assist members of clinical development with contribution to regulatory meeting preparation and interactions with global health authorities, as assigned
  • Support preparation of briefing documents, responses to agency questions, and submission documents, as assigned
  • Assist with the contribution of scientific content for INDs, CTAs, annual reports, clinical study reports, and marketing applications
  • Partner closely with Clinical Operations, Medical Affairs, Regulatory Affairs, Biometrics, Pharmacovigilance, Quality Assurance, and external 3rd party vendors including CRO partners and imaging centers
  • Support inspection readiness activities and participate in audits and regulatory inspections
  • Contribute to continuous process improvement initiatives within Clinical Development
  • Support a collaborative, high-performance culture aligned with Aurion's mission and values


ABOUT AURION BIOTECH

With offices in Seattle, Boston, and Tokyo, Aurion Biotech is a clinical-stage biotech company, whose mission is to restore vision to millions of patients with life-changing regenerative therapies. The Company’s first candidate is for the treatment of corneal edema secondary to endothelial dysfunction, and one of the first clinically validated cell therapies for corneal care; it was recently granted regulatory approval from Japan’s PMDA. Aurion Biotech is the recipient of the prestigious Prix Galien award for best start-up in biotech. The Company is preparing for clinical trials in the U.S. We are growing rapidly and seek to hire highly motivated candidates from diverse backgrounds, cultures, and experiences, who share our values:

  • Stewardship: We make the world a better place for our patients, our communities, our clinicians, and our colleagues. We act responsibly as individuals, as employees, and as a company.
  • Transformation: We embrace our challenges, our successes, and our failures. We are curious, we take risks, and we collaborate.
  • Grit: We break down walls and strive to achieve the impossible. We are persistent and resilient, and we deliver on our commitments.

Aurion Biotech has a lot to accomplish in the next few years, and this role is key to our success. Privately held, Aurion Biotech is backed by Alcon, the global leader in eye care. To learn more about Aurion Biotech, visit .


LIFE AT AURION BIOTECH

We want our people to wake up every morning excited and energized for work. We value employees, which is why we invest in making life at Aurion Biotech healthy, fun, and rewarding:

  • Robust Benefits: We offer full health insurance to employees and their families, and all the acronyms: 401(k) matching, EAP, FSA, and generous PTO.
  • Total Rewards: We offer competitive compensation packages to ensure all Aurion employees are rewarded for their hard work.
  • Perks and Fun: Paid parking, subsidized commuter passes, in-office catered lunches, team events, and community projects are just a few ways that we bond, celebrate each other, have fun, and live our values.

title: Associate Director, Statistical Programming
description:
*Local candidates based in San Diego are strongly preferred. Hybrid candidates based out of California will also be considered. *


Company Overview:


Vividion is a next generation biotechnology company based in San Diego that is leveraging its proprietary chemical proteomics platform to conduct proteome-wide footprinting of drug-protein interactions with unprecedented breadth and precision. Our technology allows us to screen, identify and optimize novel drugs that selectively bind virtually any protein, including proteins previously considered “undruggable”. Our pipeline and emerging programs reflect a matured and productive platform capable of delivering first in class drugs utilizing novel mechanisms of action (allosteric inhibitors, protein-protein interaction inhibitors, functional activators, degraders etc.) against undruggable targets in the oncology and immunology space.


We prize scientific excellence, creativity, team players and we are committed to continued innovation. We have worked hard to create a collaborative and dynamic work culture where your ideas and discoveries are valued and will have an impact. We are growing and there are opportunities for mentorship and career progression.


Vividion has been recognized as a Top Workplace by The San Diego Union-Tribune from 2022 to 2025.


Job Summary:


The Associate Director, Statistical Programming will be responsible for implementing statistical analyses using SAS and performing quality review of SAS programs and deliverables for in-house analyses as well as out-sourced programming deliverables. The incumbent is responsible for leading all the programming aspect of the project for all programming deliverables and participates in the identification and implementation of programming standards and macros to facilitate the creation of statistical deliverables. This position reports to the Director, Biostatistics and will work closely with the Biometrics Team, Clinical Operations, Regulatory, and other related disciplines, as well as CROs.
