title: Foods Vietnam DT & RTM Lead
description:
Earlier this year, Unilever announced an agreement to combine its Foods business with McCormick & Company, creating a scaled global flavour powerhouse. The proposed combination would bring together iconic Foods brands, including Hellmann’s and Knorr, with McCormick’s portfolio to create a global leader across spices, seasonings, condiments and complementary food categories, supported by strong retail and foodservice platforms. McCormick brings more than 135 years of heritage, a presence in 150+ countries and territories, and a portfolio of trusted brands. The transaction remains subject to regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions, with completion estimated for mid-2027.


JOB PURPOSE

Lead nationwide Foods Distributor Trade business, from route-to-market strategy to execution, driving delivery of Primary Sales, Secondary Sales, coverage and distribution across all regions. Ensure execution excellence and business performance through the salesforce and distributor partners, delivering Foods priorities consistently and driving sustainable growth.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Own route-to-market strategy and effectiveness: Define and continuously strengthen Foods DT route-to-market model, including coverage, distribution and service design, and determine the sizing, structure and deployment of the field force required to serve Foods effectively and efficiently across regions.
  • Build the national Foods DT plan: Translate Foods business and channel priorities into a national DT delivery plan and cascade it into clear regional objectives and actions.
  • Own sales delivery: Drive Primary Sales and Secondary Sales across all regions, run a disciplined performance rhythm to review results, identify performance gaps, and ensure timely recovery actions.
  • Lead joint business planning with distributor partners: Align targets, priorities, execution commitments and performance expectations to drive secondary sales, coverage and execution.
  • Drive national Foods DT performance: Take accountability for delivering Foods priorities across regions, partnering with the DT organization and cross-functional teams to drive portfolio, pricing, promotion, distribution and execution excellence. Maintain disciplined performance management and consistent execution standards to deliver sustainable sales and market share growth.
  • Prioritize where to win: Direct focus, resources and trade investment towards the highest-impact opportunities, while identifying and capturing new sources of growth.
  • Lead through change: Play a leading role in driving Foods DT agenda through a period of transition, helping shape and embed effective ways of working across teams and partners. Make decisions under ambiguity and sustain strong business performance as the operating model continues to evolve.
  • Build a high-performance field culture: Establish strong execution standards and field discipline across the DT organization, and build a capable, high-performing field sales force with strong ownership and a winning mindset to continuously raise the quality of execution.

EXPERIENCE & SKILLS

  • Substantial Customer Development or commercial leadership experience in FMCG or a comparable consumer business, including ownership of complex business priorities and performance delivery.
  • Strong analytical capability, with the ability to translate customer, channel and performance data into clear priorities and actions.
  • Strong leadership, stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to mobilize teams and partners behind business priorities and drive delivery across complex environments.
  • Sound planning, performance management and execution discipline, including prioritization, risk identification and timely course correction.
  • Solid understanding of route-to-market design and DT operations, including coverage, distribution, field force deployment and the commercial levers (portfolio, pricing, promotion, execution) that drive sustainable sales and market share growth.
  • Ability to lead through change, make timely decisions under ambiguity, and translate evolving priorities into effective action while maintaining strong business performance.

MINDSET & BEHAVIOURS

  • Act with integrity and sound judgment, taking ownership of decisions and outcomes.
  • Deliver performance with care, setting high standards while supporting others to succeed.
  • Prioritize what matters most, simplify complexity and focus resources on the actions that create the greatest business impact.
  • Think strategically, convert priorities into action and remain adaptable through change.

WHAT SUCCESS WILL LOOK LIKE

  • Foods business targets are consistently delivered across DT, with strong Primary Sales, Secondary Sales and market share performance.
  • Coverage, portfolio distribution and execution standards are strong and consistent across regions, with an effective route-to-market and field force model driving sustainable growth and competitive advantage.
  • Commercial resources and trade investment are focused on the highest-impact opportunities, maximizing business performance and returns.
  • The DT organization operates with strong discipline, clear priorities, and effective ways of working, enabling consistent execution and long-term growth.

We believe a diverse workforce allows us to match our growth ambitions and drive inclusion across the business. description:

JOB SUMMARY:

The City of Vestavia Hills is seeking Construction Workers to perform work that involves general or specialized duties in construction and maintenance of bridges, culverts, large pipe installation, cast in place concrete construction and other constructions projects. Work entails the use of pre-cast box culverts and pre-cast wings in the construction of bridges and culverts. Work assignments are received in the form of specific instruction pertaining to desired results and work safety methods. Employees in this classification receive continuing or individual assignments by the supervisor generally indicating work to be done, limitations, quality and quantity expected, deadlines, and priority of assignments. Employees are given additional specific instructions for new, difficult, or unusual assignments by the supervisor. Employees use initiative in carrying out recurring assignments independently without specific instructions. Work is reviewed by observation of results obtained through on-site inspection by an inspector; the supervisor assures that the work is technically accurate and in compliance with instructions, established procedures, and guidelines.

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS:

The City of Vestavia Hills provides competitive pay and comprehensive benefits packages to include medical and dental insurance, employer-sponsored retirement plan (pension), generous paid holidays, sick and vacation leave, and more. The pay range for this job is presented below:

$20.15 - $31.26

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

The following are job-related qualifications that are required for employment consideration for this position:

  • Work experience pouring and finishing concrete (e.g., sidewalks, curb and gutter, slabs).
  • Work experience using hand tools and power tools to build vertical and horizontal forms for concrete work.
  • Work experience laying masonry (e.g., mixing mortor, laying brick and/or block).


TYPICAL JOB DUTIES:

  • Leads the layout, construction, and maintenance of bridges and box culverts by directing the use of power tools, construction equipment, and concrete work in order to ensure safe roadways and properly channel the flow of water under roadways.

  • Leads the building, erection, and removal of wooden forms made of plywood, 2x4’s, or other form types by directing the use of tools such as hammers, power saws, tape measures, levels, and framing squares in order to prepare for precise concrete pours.

  • Leads the fabrication of steel cages to be placed inside forms in order to reinforce and stabilize concrete structures.

  • Leads the mixing, pouring, and finishing of concrete to construct a variety of structures (e.g., wing walls, head walls, sidewalks, driveways, slabs, retaining walls, building foundations, curbs and gutters, and drop-inlets) in order to complete construction projects to specification.

  • Participates and assists in the installation of guardrails by following Department of Transportation guidelines and project specifications, using hand tools, power tools, and guardrail components in order to enhance highway safety.

  • Maintains a safe work environment by consistently wearing appropriate protective equipment and adhering to established safety guidelines in order to ensure the safety of personnel, the public, and equipment.

  • Constructs brick and concrete block headwalls by preparing footings, mixing mortar, and laying masonry to prevent erosion around pipes, stabilize banks, and hold backfill around culverts or cross drains.

  • Acts as a lead worker of peer or support staff by assigning and reviewing work tasks, facilitating training, and providing feedback using policies, procedures, tools, and directives from management in order to ensure tasks are completed in accordance with established requirements.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS:

Job involves moderate physical exertion required for occasional prolonged periods of lifting, carrying, balancing, climbing, stooping, kneeling, crouching, or crawling. Job may involve occasional lifting of items or objects weighing more than 50 lbs.

WORK ENVIRONMENT:

Work is primarily performed at outdoor worksites such as roadways and construction sites. Work involves use of standard office equipment, such as computer, phone, copier, etc. Work may also involve the use of various hand tools such as hammer, screwdrivers, wrenches, etc. Workers may be exposed to weather conditions, such as extreme hot or cold temperatures, or other potentially hazardous conditions such as near bodies of water, earth excavations, and roadway traffic.

title: Measure Technician / Independent Contractor
description:
Position Overview
Floor Interior Services (FIS) is seeking professional, dependable Measure Technicians to perform accurate in-home flooring measurements and deliver an exceptional customer experience.
This is an independent contractor opportunity. The Measure Technician will visit customers’ homes, evaluate project conditions, accurately measure all applicable areas, document project requirements, upload completed information, and provide the customer with an in-home installation quote.
This role is more than measuring rooms. The technician is often the customer’s first face-to-face interaction with our installation team and must represent FIS with professionalism, confidence, accuracy, and urgency.

Key Responsibilities
• Travel to scheduled customer appointments within the assigned service area.
• Contact customers before arrival and maintain professional communication regarding appointment timing.
• Arrive on time, professionally dressed, and prepared to complete the assignment.
• Accurately measure rooms, closets, stairs, transitions, doorways, and other applicable installation areas.
• Identify flooring types, subfloor conditions, transitions, furniture requirements, removal needs, installation challenges, and other project-specific details.
• Create accurate diagrams, room layouts, measurements, photographs, and supporting documentation.
• Ensure all required project information is complete before leaving the customer’s home.
• Upload measurements, diagrams, photographs, notes, and other required documentation within established timelines.
• Review the proposed installation scope with the customer and provide an accurate in-home quote using company-approved systems and pricing.
• Clearly explain the installation process, anticipated requirements, and next steps without making unauthorized promises.
• Answer customer questions professionally and help create confidence in moving forward with the project.
• Immediately report safety concerns, unusual site conditions, system issues, or potential scope problems.
• Protect customer information and maintain confidentiality.
• Correct measurement or documentation errors promptly when responsible for the original assignment.

Performance Expectations
Success in this role will be measured by:
• Measurement accuracy
• Quote accuracy and completeness
• On-time appointment arrival
• Timely data and documentation uploads
• Customer satisfaction
• Quote participation and conversion results
• Professional communication
• Low remeasure and correction rates
• Compliance with FIS and retail-partner requirements
Accuracy is non-negotiable. A rushed or incomplete measurement creates problems for the customer, installer, retailer, and company. Measure twice, upload once—the tape measure has no sympathy.

Required Qualifications
• Experience in flooring measurement, flooring installation, construction, estimating, in-home sales, or a related field is preferred.
• Strong mathematical, measuring, and spatial-reasoning skills.
• Ability to learn and accurately use electronic measuring and quoting systems.
• Comfortable presenting pricing and speaking directly with customers in their homes.
• Strong attention to detail and commitment to completing documentation correctly.
• Professional appearance, communication, and customer-service skills.
• Dependable transportation and willingness to travel throughout the assigned territory.
• Smartphone, tablet, or other required technology capable of running company-approved applications.
• Ability to work independently, manage appointments, and meet established deadlines.
• Ability to pass any required background screening.
• Valid driver’s license and appropriate automobile insurance.
• Ability to meet all applicable independent contractor, licensing, insurance, and business requirements.

Physical Requirements
• Ability to walk, bend, kneel, climb stairs, and move throughout occupied and unoccupied homes.
• Ability to carry and operate measuring equipment and related technology.
• Ability to safely access rooms, closets, stairs, exterior areas, and other project spaces.
• Ability to work in homes with pets, dust, construction activity, or limited climate control.
Independent Contractor Relationship
This position is offered on an independent contractor basis. The contractor is responsible for their own transportation, equipment, insurance, taxes, business expenses, and compliance with applicable laws and contractual requirements.
Nothing in this description creates an employment relationship. Final expectations, compensation, service territory, scheduling requirements, performance standards, and contractor obligations will be governed by the applicable independent contractor agreement.

Ideal Candidate
The ideal Measure Technician is accurate, organized, technologically capable, comfortable with customers, and confident discussing project pricing. They understand that every appointment is both a technical assignment and a customer-service opportunity.
We are looking for someone who can measure the project correctly, document it completely, explain it clearly, and leave the customer feeling confident about moving forward.

title: Senior Cyberspace Operations Planner, Site Lead
description:
Looking for an opportunity to make an impact?


At Leidos, we deliver innovative solutions through the efforts of our diverse and talented people who are dedicated to our customers’ success. We empower our teams, contribute to our communities, and operate sustainably. Everything we do is built on a commitment to do the right thing for our customers, our people, and our community. The Leidos Intelligence Sector combines technology-enabled services and mission software capabilities in the areas of cyber, logistics, security operations, and decision analytics to support our defense and intel customers’ mission to defend against evolving threats around the world.


Your greatest work is ahead!


The Intelligence Sector seeks Subject Matter Expert-level Joint Cyberspace Operational Planners to serve as Site Leads within United States Cyber Command (USCYBERCOM). Individuals will provide expert guidance and direction to planning activities that underpin USCYBERCOM Cyberspace Operational Support Services (COSS) program, leading Operational Planning portion of Leidos on-site contract support to range of services provided to USCYBERCOM Operations directorate (J3), Cyber National Mission Force (CNMF), and Joint Task Force-Ares (JTF-ARES). Timely and comprehensive operational planning support to USCYBERCOM J3, CNMF, and JTF-ARES will inform employment of available Cyberspace capabilities, development of future Cyberspace capabilities, and drive the Joint Planning and Targeting processes.


What you’ll be doing:

  • Provide subject matter expertise in Joint Cyberspace plans development and staffing processes within collaborative environment to enable range of Cyberspace Operations (CO) according to USCYBERCOM planning guidance and applicable Joint publications.
  • Perform role as contract Site Lead within USCYERCOM J3, CNMF, or JTF-ARES, advising staff and leading daily activities to meet program requirements and drive USCYBERCOM mission.
  • Support targeting selection, validation, synchronization, and enable integration during the execution of activities within Cyber Warfare domain.
  • Draft and staff foundational planning documents such as Operational Plans (OPLANS), Operational Orders (OPORDs), and Fragmentary Orders (FRAGOs).
  • Support Joint Operational Planning Groups and Teams (OPG/OPT), and develop and integrate Cyber capabilities into plans.
  • Coordinate CO planning activities through the IJSTO to include Evaluation Request and Response Messages, SAP procedures, and the RAPCO.

What does Leidos need from me?

  • Active Top Secret/SCI (TS/SCI) security clearance with Counterintelligence (CI) Polygraph required. Must be SCI eligible.
  • 10 plus years’ experience as Joint Operations Planner or leading Joint Operations Planning processes, to include working knowledge of JPP, JOPES, and APEX planning guidance.
  • Total years’ experience as Joint Operations Planner can be mitigated by completion of advanced service-specific planning schools such as SAMS, SAWS, and JAWS.
  • 10 plus years active within field of Cyber or 15 plus years combined experience within fields of Cyber, Intelligence, Electronic Warfare, Information Technology or related fields, with preference for combination leadership and hands-on experience over the course of career.
  • Experience leading teams and providing senior-level advice to organizational leadership within USCYBERCOM J3, CNMF, or JTF-ARES across both Offensive Cyberspace and Defensive Operations lines of effort.
  • Recipient of specialized education in military joint operations planning through JPME Level II.
  • Possess deep familiarity with military operations including phases of planning, approval, and execution.
  • Intimate familiarity with applicable Joint Publications such as JP 5-0 Joint Operational Planning.
  • Graduate of formal training as Cyber Operational Planner within Department of Defense or Intelligence Community.
  • Broad knowledge of Blue-space Cyber capabilities and demonstrate understanding of available Cyber infrastructure or platforms to conduct CO.
  • Deep knowledge of the range of CO and their underlying intelligence support needs, topics, and focus areas, and computer networking fundamentals as well as concepts, terminology, and operations of a wide range of communications media (computer and telephone networks, satellite, fiber, wireless).

Favorable if you have:

  • BA/BS or Masters’ Degree within STEM field, National Security Studies, or field of study supporting operational art and science.
  • Active Project Management Professional (PMP) certification or equivalent.
  • Deep familiarity with USCYBERCOM organizational structure and mission.
  • Prior experience supporting Joint operations across multiple warfighting domains.
  • Demonstrated experience incorporating Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning into operations at any level to increase efficiency and effectiveness of operational outcomes.
  • Experience with Space-enabled CO.
  • Formal training within field of Cyber Warfare and Joint Operations

Clinic Director

Ellie Mental Health – Portsmouth-Seacoast, New Hampshire

The Opportunity

Ellie Mental Health Portsmouth-Seacoast is seeking a licensed Clinic Practice Manager to lead and continue building our established outpatient mental health practice in Portsmouth, New Hampshire.

This is an opportunity for an experienced clinician who wants more than a traditional therapy or clinical supervision role. We are looking for someone who wants to lead a clinical team, shape the culture of the practice, mentor and develop clinicians, uphold exceptional standards of client care, and take meaningful responsibility for building a practice that is clinically strong, financially sustainable, collaborative, and positioned for continued growth.

Have you ever wanted to lead and build a mental health practice without taking on the financial risk and start-up costs of ownership? This role offers meaningful leadership and autonomy combined with the infrastructure and support of an established practice.

You will work in partnership with the Franchise Owners while having substantial responsibility for the day-to-day leadership and performance of the clinic. You'll have the opportunity to focus on people, clinical quality, practice performance, community relationships, and growth while benefiting from established systems and resources for billing, credentialing, HR, payroll, marketing, technology, and administrative processes.

Why This Role Is Different

Clinicians who want to move into meaningful leadership often face two choices: remain primarily clinical with limited ability to influence how a practice operates, or assume the financial risk and administrative burden of building a private practice themselves.

We believe there is another option.

As Clinic Practice Manager, you will have the opportunity to:

  • Lead and develop an established and growing clinical team.

  • Shape the culture, standards, and direction of the practice.

  • Recruit, mentor, coach, and retain exceptional clinicians.

  • Provide clinical supervision and professional development.

  • Maintain a small, intentional clinical caseload.

  • Take meaningful responsibility for the operational and financial performance of the practice.

  • Build relationships within the Seacoast community and develop new referral opportunities.

  • Partner directly with the Franchise Owners on strategy, growth, and the future direction of the practice.

  • Lead with meaningful autonomy while benefiting from established administrative and operational resources.

This is not a private practice ownership position, but it is also not a low-responsibility management role. It is designed for someone who wants genuine leadership, accountability, autonomy, and the opportunity to help build something meaningful.

What Success Looks Like

Success in this role means building and maintaining a practice where both clients and clinicians can thrive.

We will look to the Clinic Practice Manager to help create:

  • A stable, engaged, accountable, and growing clinical team.

  • Strong clinical supervision, mentorship, and professional development.

  • Consistently high standards for clinical care, ethics, documentation, and client experience.

  • A positive workplace culture where clinicians feel both supported and accountable.

  • Healthy clinician caseloads and strong productivity.

  • Strong client access, satisfaction, and retention.

  • Effective partnership and communication between clinical leadership and Franchise Owners.

  • Responsible financial performance and sustainable practice growth.

  • Strong referral relationships and a meaningful presence within the Portsmouth-Seacoast community.

Who We're Looking For

We are looking for a clinically strong, grounded, and motivated leader who genuinely enjoys developing people and wants to take responsibility for the success of a mental health practice.

The ideal candidate:

  • Wants to lead, mentor, coach, and develop clinicians.

  • Has strong clinical judgment, professional boundaries, and ethical standards.

  • Communicates clearly, directly, and constructively.

  • Can hold people accountable while maintaining a supportive and positive culture.

  • Is comfortable having difficult conversations and addressing problems rather than avoiding them.

  • Values collaboration while also being comfortable making decisions.

  • Understands that a healthy practice requires excellent clinical care and sound business practices.

  • Is comfortable working with performance metrics, productivity expectations, financial information, and operational goals.

  • Is proactive, resourceful, and willing to roll up their sleeves when something needs to get done.

  • Enjoys identifying problems and developing practical solutions.

  • Values clinical autonomy while recognizing the importance of partnership and alignment with ownership.

  • Wants to build something meaningful and take pride in the results.

Qualifications

Required

  • Master's or Doctoral degree in an appropriate behavioral health discipline.

  • Current, unrestricted New Hampshire clinical license in good standing as an LCMHC, LICSW, or Licensed Psychologist.

  • Minimum of five years of professional experience related to the responsibilities of the position.

  • Experience in outpatient mental health, group practice, community mental health, or a comparable clinical environment.

  • Strong clinical judgment and understanding of ethical and professional standards.

  • Ability to supervise, mentor, coach, and develop clinicians.

  • Strong leadership, communication, documentation, and organizational skills.

  • Ability to understand and work with clinical, operational, financial, and performance data.

Preferred

  • Previous experience as a Clinic Director, Practice Manager, Clinical Supervisor, Program Director, Lead Clinician, or similar leadership role.

  • Experience supervising clinicians working toward independent licensure.

  • Experience recruiting, building, scaling, or stabilizing a clinical team.

  • Experience managing employee performance and developing high-performing teams.

  • Familiarity with outpatient mental health practice operations.

  • Experience with practice financials, productivity metrics, budgeting, or performance management.

  • Interest or experience in community partnerships, referral development, and practice growth.

Compensation & Benefits

  • Base salary: $80,000–$110,000, commensurate with experience, qualifications, leadership responsibilities, and clinical contribution.

  • Performance-based bonus opportunity tied to achievement of established clinic goals.

  • Additional commission opportunity based on clinical services, as applicable.

  • Health insurance.

  • 401(k).

  • Paid time off.

  • Professional leadership and growth opportunities as the practice expands.

  • Established operational and administrative infrastructure designed to allow the Clinic Practice Manager to focus on leadership, people, clinical excellence, and practice performance.

About Ellie Mental Health

Ellie Mental Health was founded on the belief that mental healthcare should be accessible, human, and sustainable—for both clients and clinicians.

Our model is designed to reduce unnecessary barriers, support clinicians, and create an environment where high-quality mental health care can thrive.

Ellie Mental Health Portsmouth-Seacoast is locally owned and operated. This provides our team with the benefits and resources of an established national organization while preserving local leadership, decision-making, relationships, and investment in the community we serve.

Our six core values—authenticity, humor, compassion, creativity, acceptance, and determination—guide how we care for our clients, work with one another, and approach the challenges facing mental healthcare.

At the end of the day, we're people helping people. If that sounds like the kind of practice you'd like to help lead, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Construction Project Manager - Jefferson County (General Services)
description:
TARGET CLOSE DATE:

11/06/2026

PAY GRADE:

Grade 29

TYPE:

Full time

JOB SUMMARY:

Jefferson County is seeking well-qualified Construction Project Managers for its General Services department. Construction Project Managers oversee the planning, coordination, execution, and completion of construction, renovation, repair, and infrastructure improvement projects for their assigned jurisdiction. Employees in this job class manage multiple projects through various phases, including project development, budgeting, procurement, construction, and closeout. Construction Project Managers coordinate the activities of contractors, consultants, engineers, architects, and internal project teams to ensure work is completed according to approved plans, specifications, schedules, budgets, and applicable regulations. Employees exercise independent judgment in managing project resources, resolving construction-related issues, monitoring project performance, and recommending corrective actions. Construction Project Managers report to a higher-level manager or department head and may serve as lead workers by providing work direction and technical guidance to assigned personnel.

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS:

Jefferson County provides competitive pay and comprehensive benefits packages to include medical and dental insurance, employer-sponsored retirement plan (pension), generous paid holidays, sick and vacation leave, and more. The pay range for this job is presented below:

$80,288 - $124,571

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

The following are job-related qualifications that are required for employment consideration for this position.

  • Experience managing construction, renovation, or infrastructure improvement projects, such as developing project scopes, preparing construction schedules, coordinating contractors and subcontractors, allocating materials and equipment, monitoring construction progress, or overseeing project completion.
  • Experience developing or managing construction project budgets, such as preparing construction cost estimates, tracking labor and material expenses, monitoring project expenditures, evaluating cost overruns, forecasting project costs, or recommending budget adjustments.
  • Experience participating in construction procurement (e.g., preparing bid documents, evaluating contractor proposals, coordinating contractor selection) or administering construction contracts (e.g., monitoring contractor performance, reviewing payment applications, processing change orders, ensuring compliance with contract requirements).

TARGETED QUALIFICATIONS:

The following job-related qualification is deemed desirable by Jefferson County. This qualification may be considered by a hiring agency when reviewing applications and inviting candidates to participate in subsequent steps in the selection process.

  • Bachelor’s degree or higher in engineering, construction management, building science, or a closely related field.

TYPICAL JOB DUTIES:

  • Develops construction, renovation, and infrastructure improvement project plans by assessing site conditions, consulting with stakeholders, reviewing historical project information, and establishing project scopes, budgets, schedules, resource requirements, and contingency measures in accordance with departmental priorities and approved project objectives to guide projects from initial development through completion.
  • Manages multiple construction projects through planning, design, construction, and completion by coordinating project activities, establishing priorities, allocating resources, monitoring milestones, and adjusting project schedules in accordance with approved plans, contractual requirements, and departmental procedures to ensure projects are completed efficiently, on schedule, and within budget.
  • Oversees construction activities and contractor performance by conducting site visits, reviewing inspection reports, evaluating work progress, and comparing completed work against project plans and specifications in accordance with applicable building codes, safety regulations, contractual requirements, and quality standards to identify deficiencies, resolve construction problems, and ensure acceptable workmanship.
  • Administers construction and professional service contracts by preparing procurement documentation, evaluating bids and proposals, coordinating contractor selection, reviewing contractual deliverables, processing payment requests, and evaluating change orders in accordance with applicable purchasing regulations, contractual provisions, and delegated approval authority to ensure compliance with contract requirements and appropriate use of project funds.
  • Manages construction project budgets and resources by preparing cost estimates, monitoring expenditures, reviewing financial reports, coordinating personnel and equipment needs, and evaluating proposed cost adjustments in accordance with approved funding allocations and established financial procedures to maintain cost control and support efficient resource utilization across assigned projects.
  • Coordinates construction project activities with architects, engineers, contractors, consultants, government agencies, internal departments, and other stakeholders by conducting project meetings, reviewing technical documents, responding to inquiries, and communicating project requirements and changes in accordance with established communication procedures to resolve coordination issues and maintain progress toward project objectives.
  • Monitors and documents construction project performance by tracking schedules, expenditures, milestones, contract compliance, and outstanding issues; preparing project status reports; and coordinating final inspections, corrective work, and closeout documentation in accordance with departmental reporting requirements and contractual provisions to inform management, support project acceptance, and maintain complete project records.
  • Serves as a lead worker for assigned construction project personnel by coordinating daily work activities, distributing assignments, monitoring work progress, providing technical guidance, and assisting with problem-solving in accordance with project plans, established procedures, and departmental priorities to support employee performance and effective project execution.
  • Maintains knowledge of construction management practices, building codes, safety regulations, procurement requirements, and emerging industry standards by reviewing professional publications, attending training programs, and participating in professional development activities in accordance with departmental expectations to support effective project management and regulatory compliance.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS:

Job is primarily sedentary, involving sitting for extended periods, but requires occasional walking, standing, bending, stooping, crouching, and climbing stairs or ladders when visiting construction sites, and may involve walking on uneven or unstable surfaces and occasional lifting or carrying of materials or equipment weighing up to 25 lbs.

WORK ENVIRONMENT:

Work is conducted primarily indoors in an office setting using standard office equipment, with occasional travel to construction sites, buildings under construction or renovation, and other project locations. Construction site visits may involve exposure to uneven surfaces, inclement weather, dust, noise, moving equipment, and other construction-related hazards requiring the use of appropriate personal protective equipment (e.g., hard hats, safety glasses, safety footwear).

This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment with the Personnel Board of Jefferson County, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training. Each Merit System member city/agency operates its own equal employment opportunity policies available on the individual city/agency website.

ACCOMMODATION:

To request an accommodation in the application or hiring process due to your own ongoing medical condition or disability, please contact our Accommodations Coordinator at accommodationrequest@pbjcal.org or phone at 205-279-3500 (select option 1) Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Central Time. The accommodation process is reserved solely for job seekers with disabilities requesting accessibility assistance or accommodation in the job application process.

title: Network Order Entry Specialist
description:
At The One 23 Group, our mission is to set the benchmark for excellence in government services. With our global footprint, we place a strong emphasis on nurturing our people and culture, which forms the core of our successful strategies in leadership and financial management. We pride ourselves on our extensive experience and effective approach, ensuring that we lead with both innovation and integrity.


THE POSITION

The Network Order Entry Specialist for DISN Consolidated Provisioning (DCP) will support the provisioning lifecycle throughout the order entry, order preparation, solution design, and circuit activation phases. This professional will also participate in customer outreach support, Quality of Service (QoS) configuration, commercial leasing support and facilities engineering in support.


RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Enter and update configuration and administrative changes in the configuration management database.
  • Identify and allocate building components, modules, ports, virtual interfaces and/or cross-connections.
  • Maintain non-conforming circuit lists for those circuits that do not have a viable technical solution available.
  • Support DISA projects using existing and/or future Government configuration management databases to develop and maintain comprehensive lists of circuits, known as Master Circuit Lists (MCLs), and trunks that are impacted by the project.
  • Develop Method of Precedence or Procedure (MOP) to detail how circuits are transitioned based on redundancy, hot cuts, and identifies critical dependencies.
  • Track the status of service requests, MCLs, and CTPs in the Government provided tracking repository.
  • the progress of critical requirements within the prescribed timeframe.

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

  • On-site in Columbus, OH.
  • Day shift with occasional flexibility for swing or alternate hours as needed.

title: Commercial Project Delivery Manager - Solar & Battery
description:
Benefits:

  • Paid time off
  • 401(k) matching

Help Lead the Next Chapter of One of the Region's Most Respected Solar Companies

For more than 20 years, Exact Solar has built a reputation as one of the Mid-Atlantic region's most trusted solar companies through technical excellence, exceptional customer service, and a genuine commitment to our employees.

As our business continues to grow, we are seeking an experienced Commercial Project Delivery Manager to join our operations team and help support the successful execution of an expanding portfolio of commercial solar projects.

This is not a traditional project management role. We're looking for someone who enjoys making an entire organization stronger. Someone who naturally asks:

"How can I help this team succeed?"

If you're energized by leading commercial solar projects, supporting field teams, improving operational coordination, developing people, and helping a growing company scale successfully, we'd love to meet you.

About the Role

As Exact Solar has grown, so has the complexity and volume of the projects we deliver. We already have an experienced operations team, including our Master Electrician who oversees our commercial field operations and has been instrumental in building our reputation for quality.

However, we are hoping to find a seasoned project or construction management professional to increase our operational capacity and provide the additional bandwidth needed to support a growing organization. This is a local, in-office, in-person role in Newtown, PA. Remote candidates will not be considered.

Working directly alongside our Operations Leadership Team and ownership, you will help coordinate commercial project delivery from engineering through commissioning while supporting hiring, workforce planning, scheduling, procurement, engineering coordination, customer communication, and field execution. Together, you'll help ensure our operations continue to scale without compromising the quality, craftsmanship, customer experience, or team culture that define Exact Solar.

Your Primary Responsibilities

Working in partnership with our Operations Leader, you will help coordinate all aspects of commercial project delivery and operational execution.

Commercial Project Delivery

  • Lead commercial solar projects from contract turnover through final commissioning.

  • Coordinate engineering, permitting, procurement, scheduling, construction, inspections, commissioning, and project closeout.

  • Develop and maintain project schedules, budgets, milestones, and action plans.

  • Proactively identify and resolve project challenges before they impact schedule, quality, or customer satisfaction.

  • Manage customer communications throughout project execution.

  • Coordinate with utility companies, inspectors, AHJs, engineering partners, and subcontractors.

  • Support project financial performance through effective planning and execution.

Field Leadership & Coordination

  • Spend regular time in the field supporting superintendents, foremen, electricians, subcontractors, inspectors, and customers.

  • Help remove obstacles so field teams can remain productive and focused on quality workmanship.

  • Coordinate field activities, site logistics, equipment deliveries, and project milestones.

  • Support safety, quality assurance, and commissioning activities.

  • Assist with workforce planning and crew utilization.

Operations Support

As a key member of our operations leadership team, you'll help provide additional management bandwidth in areas including:

  • Workforce planning and hiring

  • Recruiting and onboarding new team members

  • Scheduling crews and subcontractors

  • Procurement and long-lead equipment planning

  • Engineering and design coordination

  • Utility interconnection and inspection coordination

  • Inventory planning and forecasting

  • Resource planning and workload forecasting

  • Continuous improvement initiatives

  • Process development and operational coordination

This role is highly collaborative. Rather than operating independently, you'll work alongside existing leadership to improve communication, coordination, and execution across the organization.

Required Qualifications

  • Minimum five years of commercial solar project management experience.

  • Demonstrated experience managing commercial photovoltaic projects from contract award through commissioning.

  • Experience managing field personnel, construction superintendents, foremen, subcontractors, and installation crews on active job sites.

  • Strong understanding of commercial solar construction, electrical systems, scheduling, procurement, safety, inspections, and commissioning.

  • Experience coordinating engineering, permitting, utility interconnection, and AHJ inspections.

  • Strong organizational, planning, and problem-solving skills.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

  • Strong proficiency with Microsoft Excel and project management software.

  • Ability to manage multiple projects and priorities simultaneously.

  • Valid driver's license and willingness to travel regularly to project sites throughout our service territory.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Construction Management, Business, or a related field.

  • NABCEP certification or other renewable energy credentials.

  • Experience with commercial battery storage projects.

  • Experience with ERP, scheduling, or project management platforms.

Who We're Looking For

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys collaborating with experienced professionals rather than working independently in a silo.

The strongest candidates will be comfortable moving between the office and the field, helping solve problems wherever they're needed—whether that's reviewing engineering progress, walking a jobsite with a foreman, coordinating equipment deliveries, assisting with hiring, or helping ownership think several months ahead.

More than anything, we're looking for a servant leadership personality. Someone who:

  • Builds trust before making changes.

  • Leads through collaboration rather than authority.

  • Enjoys helping others become more successful.

  • Listens first and acts thoughtfully.

  • Earns respect through competence, humility, and consistency.

  • Values teamwork over ego.

title: Bailff/Court Security
description:
TARGET CLOSE DATE:

11/06/2026

PAY GRADE:

Grade 15

TYPE:

Full time

JOB SUMMARY:

Bailiff/Court Security personnel in the Merit System are responsible for facilitating court operations and ensuring the safety of visitors, employees, confined persons, and the general public within courthouse and courtroom environments. Employees in this job class perform a variety of duties related to courtroom operations and security, including preparing courtrooms for sessions, guarding prisoners, screening visitors and their possessions upon entry to the courthouse, maintaining order in courtrooms, and completing and filing paperwork from court cases.

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS:

Agencies provide competitive pay and comprehensive benefits packages to include medical and dental insurance, employer-sponsored retirement plan (pension), generous paid holidays, sick and vacation leave, and more.

Applications for this position will be considered for the following Merit System employing agencies. The pay range for this job varies depending upon the Merit System employing agency.

Bessemer $16.64 - $25.82
Birmingham $17.00 - $26.37
Hueytown $18.03 - $27.97
Jefferson County $19.50 - $30.25

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

The following are job-related qualifications that are required for employment consideration for this position:

  • Driver's license.
  • Ability to legally carry a firearm.
  • Willing and able to obtain a pepper spray certification within 90 days of hire, if required by the hiring jurisdiction.
  • Willingness to work in a hostile environment.
  • Willingness to use physical agility to restrain and/or detain individuals.

TYPICAL JOB DUTIES:

  • Prepares, maintains, and retrieves files to assist court officers before and during court sessions (e.g., collects and provides files to the judge as defendants go before the judge, completes various paperwork from cases, maintains statistical records on cases heard and attendance rates).

  • Prepares courtroom for hearings (e.g., ensures cleanliness, prepares packets of forms goes over docket, arranges furniture) and administers the flow of defendants through the hearing process (e.g., reads defendant rights, instructs on rules of courtroom procedure) and announces commencement of court sessions.

  • Provides customer service, internally and/or externally, via phone, email or face to face interaction.

  • Engages in activities designed to ensure professional development, awareness of developments in the field, and knowledge of relevant practices, rules, laws, policies, and/or guidelines.

  • Provides security to the presiding judge and those in attendance, explains/enforces rules and regulations that govern the activities of all people entering the courtroom so court can proceed efficiently and safely.

  • Announces the commencement of court sessions by explaining court procedures, defendants’ rights and penalties, etc. to ensure all in attendance comprehend the proceedings.

  • Answers phone calls in order to provide general information (e.g., operation hours) and forward messages to appropriate personnel.

  • Restrains individuals and escorts them out of court upon judge's directive to de-escalate the situation.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS:

Job involves physical exertion required for sustained period of light physical activity such as walking or standing, and may occasionally require significant and concerted physical exertion for the purposes of restraining and/or detaining individuals in court and surrounding areas. Job may require applying self-defense and restraint tactics to defend oneself from physical attack.

WORK ENVIRONMENT:

Work is conducted primarily in courtroom and office settings. Work may involve the use of pepper spray, pistols, and a variety of restraint devices. May be required to work/deal with angry, physically aggressive, or violent individuals, and thus, may be exposed to potential and real physical violence. Employees in this class may also be required to work during lunch, or after normal working hours.

DMR is building next-generation drone technology right here in Lafayette, LA. Our flight controllers are flying production missions today — multi-IMU redundancy, dual GPS+RTK, dual-antenna heading with magnetometer fusion, and layered safety strategies. We need a firmware engineer ready to own this system, push it forward, and help us scale.


What You'll Do

• Own the flight control firmware — analyze, document, and evolve a mature production codebase covering multi-IMU redundancy, dual GPS+RTK, and dual-antenna heading fusion.

• Lead feature development and stability tuning for RTK and 4G modules.

• Develop and maintain sensor drivers: IMU, GNSS, magnetic compass, barometer, Hall/ultrasonic flow meters, and radar.

• Implement production-line calibration methods and support test fixtures.

• Maintain the flight control protocol SDK; coordinate integration with application and cloud teams.

• Refine flight modes and safety strategies; contribute early research into RTK base stations and centrifugal nozzles.

• Close the loop on mass-production issues and ensure firmware consistency across batches.




What You Bring

• Bachelor's degree or above in Automation, Electronics, Aerospace, Computer Science, or related field.

• 5+ years of embedded flight control firmware experience, including at least one drone controller taken from development through mass production.

• Strong STM32 (H7 preferred) skills — both bare-metal and RTOS environments.

• Solid knowledge of IMU/GNSS-RTK/compass drivers and multi-sensor fusion (Kalman/ESKF), attitude estimation, and control algorithms.

• Familiarity with CAN, RS-485, serial, PWM, ADC, and other embedded bus interfaces.

• Self-directed — you can troubleshoot independently and drive work to completion.




Bonus Points

title: Driving Instructor - TX
description:
CLICK THE CITY & STATE ABOVE TO VIEW OUR EXACT LOCATION


About us

Coastline Academy is the largest and fastest growing driving school in the country. Since 2017 we've taught more than 250,000 students across seven states, backed by over 100,000 five-star reviews.

We're on a mission to eradicate car crashes by teaching safe and confident drivers for life. We're people-first and technology-centric: online booking, digital lesson reports, transparent pricing, modern cars. 98% of our students rate their lesson five stars.

Become part of a team committed to creating safe, confident drivers for life.


About this role

You'll sit in the passenger seat of a Coastline car and teach people something they'll use every day for the rest of their lives. Most of your students are teenagers taking their first turn behind the wheel. Some are adults getting ready for a road test. All of them leave your car more capable than when they got in.

  • You teach in our car, not yours. Every Coastline vehicle is company-provided, clearly marked, fitted with a second instructor brake, and inspected by certified mechanics.
  • We pay for your certification. Our training team walks you through your state's driving instructor licensing requirements and provides the coursework. Training is paid.
  • Every lesson is recorded. Dashcams capture video and audio inside and outside the car for your safety and your student's.
  • Your schedule follows the students. Most of our students are in school, so demand concentrates in afternoons and weekends. A typical day is three two-hour lessons.


What does training entail?


Training Breakdown (30 Hours Total):

  • 18 Hours Virtual Learning: Self-paced reading and module completion from home.
  • 12 Hours Hands-On Driving & Practical Mentorship: Shadow 6 hours live in-car lessons (three 2-hour lesson with student) and complete 6 hours of direct coaching with a Certified Trainer (two 3-hour sessions).

You'll never be conducting lessons alone in a car with a student until you're ready.


What you'll do

  • Teach the practical skills of driving, every aspect, from parking lots to freeway merges
  • Coach students on the rules of the road
  • Build confidence, not just competence
  • Take control of the vehicle when a situation calls for it
  • Document and report on each student's progress
  • Stay in close, timely communication with your supervisor and support team
  • Bring professionalism to every interaction with students and teammates
  • Show up for team meetings, updates, and ongoing development

Technical Equipment Maintenance & Repair:

title: Drone Engineer Mandarin
description:
Drone Engineer (Mandarin Required)

DMR Technologies | Lafayette, Louisiana

Target Candidates: Louisiana and Texas
Disciplines: Mechanical, Electrical, Aerospace, Mechatronics Engineering

About DMR Technologies

DMR Technologies is a Louisiana-based drone technology company focused on the development, manufacturing, and commercialization of advanced unmanned aircraft systems (UAS).

As we expand our U.S. engineering and manufacturing capabilities, we are seeking a technically capable Drone Engineer who can support product development, engineering coordination, and the transition of advanced drone technologies into American manufacturing operations.

Position Overview

The Drone Engineer will serve as a critical technical link between DMR's U.S. operations and external engineering partners.

This position requires a strong foundation in mechanical, electrical, aerospace, or mechatronics engineering, along with conversational Mandarin proficiency to facilitate effective communication across international engineering teams.

The ideal candidate can translate technical discussions into actionable engineering requirements, resolve design and manufacturing challenges, and support the development and localization of drone systems for the U.S. market.

Key Responsibilities

  • Coordinate technical discussions between DMR's U.S. engineering and manufacturing teams and international engineering partners.

  • Communicate effectively in English and Mandarin regarding engineering specifications, design revisions, component requirements, and technical issues.

  • Review engineering drawings, schematics, specifications, and technical documentation.

  • Support mechanical, electrical, and systems integration of unmanned aircraft.

  • Assist with design improvements, prototyping, testing, troubleshooting, and validation.

  • Translate engineering requirements into actionable instructions for U.S. manufacturing and assembly teams.

  • Identify opportunities to improve product reliability, manufacturability, serviceability, and performance.

  • Support engineering change management, documentation, and quality control processes.

  • Collaborate with operations, supply chain, and product development personnel to resolve technical challenges.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Mechatronics, or a closely related field.

  • Conversational proficiency in Mandarin Chinese required, including the ability to understand and participate in technical discussions.

  • Strong professional English communication skills.

  • Working knowledge of U.S. engineering practices, technical documentation, and manufacturing processes.

  • Ability to interpret engineering drawings, technical specifications, and design documentation.

  • Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and cross-functional communication skills.

  • Ability to work on-site in Lafayette, Louisiana.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with unmanned aircraft systems, robotics, aerospace, or electromechanical products.

  • Familiarity with CAD software, electrical schematics, embedded systems, or flight-control architecture.

  • Experience working with international engineering or manufacturing teams.

  • Knowledge of design for manufacturing (DFM), engineering change orders (ECOs), and product lifecycle management.

  • Experience supporting product localization or U.S.-based manufacturing initiatives.

  • Familiarity with FAA regulations and UAS operational requirements.

Why Join DMR?

Join a growing Louisiana technology company helping build the future of American drone manufacturing. This role offers the opportunity to work directly with company leadership, influence product development, and help establish engineering and manufacturing capabilities in the United States.

title: Volunteer & Donations Coordinator
description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

This position is represented by the OPEIU union and subject to the terms and conditions of a collective bargaining agreement.


This position has an end date of January 08, 2027.


Job Overview: The Volunteer and Donations Coordinator is the community engagement focal point for each office and serves a critical systems support role connecting the talents & resources of the community to meet client needs & programmatic compliance. This role coordinates volunteer & intern support, financial & in-kind donations, as well as communications and outreach. The coordinator will recruit volunteers & interns and design effective volunteer opportunities to support core IRC programming while maintaining donations through procurement, management, and distribution of in-kind contributions from our community of supporters. In addition to volunteer and donations coordination, this role is essential in supporting the overall messaging of the office, including creating branded visuals and content for Facebook, the website, and newsletters. The Volunteer and Donations Coordinator will coordinate external community engagement events and support corporate relations activities. This role plays a key part in advancing the Development and Fundraising strategy for the Northern California region, strengthening community partnerships, expanding donor and volunteer engagement, and enhancing resource mobilization to support IRC’s mission.


Major Responsibilities:

Volunteer Recruitment & Management

  • Develop and implement recruitment strategies, including partnerships with universities, faith-based groups, and community organizations.
  • Screen, orient, and match volunteers and interns with appropriate service opportunities.
  • Collaborate with staff to create and maintain up-to-date service descriptions for all volunteer and internship roles.
  • Conduct onboarding orientations and assist with administrative needs for all new recruits.
  • Manage volunteer engagement in alignment with IRC program objectives and national guidelines.
  • Maintain accurate records of volunteer participation, including tracking hours in the Salesforce volunteer database.
  • Ensure all placements have complete and properly documented files.
  • Recognize and appreciate volunteers through events and ongoing communication.
  • Provide ongoing support to volunteers and interns throughout their service period.
  • Implement the NorCal Volunteer and Intern Program and refine workflows to enhance the volunteer experience.

Donations Coordination & Development Support

  • Track, pursue, and report on in-kind contributions on a monthly basis in collaboration with Operations Specialists.
  • Oversee storage, inventory, and distribution of in-kind donations across IRC locations in collaboration with Operations Specialist.
  • Develop and execute a donation allocation strategy to support program needs and meet grant match requirements.
  • Collaborate with staff managing match-generating programs to allocate and distribute donations effectively.
  • Submit monthly Community In-Kind (CIK) Reports, tracking volunteer hours and the value of in-kind donations.
  • Integrate donation and volunteer activity tracking into Integra, IRC’s business database, including system development and adaptation.
  • Build partnerships with local community members to secure donations and in-kind contributions.

Community Engagement & Outreach

  • Conduct outreach to community groups, faith-based organizations, and businesses to secure volunteer support, financial and in-kind contributions, and community sponsorships.
  • Represent IRC at career fairs, fundraising events, and community outreach initiatives.
  • Plan and execute fundraising and outreach events to increase awareness and support, in alignment with NorCal’s Development Strategy.
  • Assist the NorCal Development Director in organizing corporate engagement events and executing the local office’s Corporate Engagement Menu and ensuring office meets fundraising targets.
  • Manage the office’s social media strategy, ensuring compliance with grant requirements and maintaining regular, relevant content.
  • Maintain website content related to volunteer and internship opportunities, in-kind donations, and NorCal newsletter contributions.

Staff & Program Support

  • Work with Program Managers/Coordinators to assess needs and develop recruitment strategies for volunteers and interns across key departments, including:
    • Reception & Placement
    • Economic Empowerment & Match Grant
    • Immigration Services
    • Intensive Case Management
    • Anti-Trafficking Initiatives
    • Digital Inclusion Programs
  • Train and support staff in volunteer management best practices to ensure a positive experience for volunteers and program staff.
  • Serve as the lead for all Community Engagement efforts and participate in leadership team meetings.
  • Collaborate with the Director to provide insights on volunteer engagement and community outreach initiatives.
  • Engage in IRC Communities of Practice, networking events, and professional development opportunities.
  • Perform other related duties as assigned.

Key Working Relationships:

Position Reports to: Development Director
Position directly supervises: N/A; Oversees volunteer and interns
Other Internal and/or external contacts:

Internal: Operations Specialist, Development Director, HQ Development staff, Grants Managers, direct service Program Managers, Site Directors, Executive Director

External: Local businesses, corporations, faith-based organizations, schools, and community organizations offering volunteer, cash and in-kind support.


Job Requirements:

  • Undergraduate degree required. Preferably with an emphasis in communication, non-profit management, human resources, international development or and relevant field of study.
  • Minimum of 3 years of demonstrated success in community engagement.
  • Demonstrated experience in fundraising, sponsorship solicitation, or donor cultivation, with the ability to meet assigned fundraising goals, including this role's annual targets of ~$200,000 in new revenue and ~$125,000 in Match support.
  • Excellent Microsoft Office skills and ability to learn new computer applications rapidly.
  • Deep understanding of program management and human resource management principles and experience managing diverse teams.
  • Proven ability to contribute both independently and as a key team member.
  • Demonstrated success working and communicating effectively in a multi-cultural environment.
  • Flexible and able to handle pressure well.
  • Experience developing and providing orientations and trainings.
  • Strong organizational skills in a complex, multi-tasking environment and the ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines.
  • Excellent interpersonal communication skills; ability to communicate effectively and diplomatically with current and prospective donors and volunteers, partner agencies, multi-cultural clients and colleagues on all levels.

Language Skills: Fluent in English, both spoken and written.

Working Environment

  • Standard office environment, some evening and weekend hours will be required.
  • Must have a valid driver’s license with legally required insurance as position may require using own transportation within the service delivery area. Mileage reimbursement is available.

Compensation: ($75,369 to $78,866 annually). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

Professional Standards: All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.


Cookies:


Benefits: IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.


Equal Opportunity Employer: IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Join MRPC: Build What’s Next in Medical Technology


Make an impact. Grow your career. Shape the future of healthcare.

With more than 100 years of manufacturing expertise, MRPC is a growing leader in medical device manufacturing, supporting advanced technologies like robotic-assisted surgery and next-generation healthcare solutions.

Join MRPC and build a career with purpose.


POSITION SUMMARY:

Under the general supervision of the Production Supervisor, the Process Technician is responsible for set-up & adjustment operations as per D.O.P.’s & industry accepted standards. Set up department equipment and provide work direction, training, and guidance to personnel.


ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:

This list of duties and responsibilities is not all inclusive and may be expanded as management determines necessary.

· Review work orders for the day; assign work for the shift.

· Ensure an adequate supply of materials for area operations.

· Set up department equipment and machinery to include all secondary equipment. Troubleshoot machinery.

· Schedule work for operators, train and provide guidance as required.

· Ensure that operators comply with established safety regulations and department policies.

· Perform first shot approvals using Q.A. measuring equipment

· Monitor and review production/labor reports.

· Supervise the maintenance of the cleanliness of the department.

· Perform housekeeping activities to maintain work area and assure cleanliness of environment.

· Operate equipment as needed.

· Troubleshoot jobs as necessary to maintain quality & production standards.

· Clean filters, grinders & auxiliary equipment as necessary.

· Set up molds and set adjustments following the Work Instructions or D.O. P.’s.

· Maintain the molds; clean molds in chemical solutions; perform blasting and cold jet procedures, examine for wear and defects, and forward to the tool room for repair.

· Perform SPC and press checks at required intervals.

· Follow and update DOP's for the department.

· Provide assistance to press operators on production runs; resolve production problems and troubleshoot jobs as required.

· Document parameter discrepancies to supervisor and engineering. Follow up on changes needed for processes.

· Maintain the required records and files.

· Perform supervisory activities to include work direction, scheduling, and shipping in supervisor's absence.

· Perform minor maintenance, as needed, on machines and equipment.

· Perform other duties as assigned.


QUALIFICATIONS (KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & ABILITIES):

· High school diploma or equivalent

· Requires the ability to follow written and verbal instructions

· Knowledge of press operations and shop mathematics

· Ability to operate the forklift, hoist, and various department equipment

· Perform extensive climbing and bending activities

· Requires knowledge or various types of plastic resins and compounds, and drying techniques


PHYSICAL DEMANDS & WORK ENVIRONMENT

  • Work is performed primarily on the manufacturing floor and requires standing or walking for extended periods, and the ability to lift up to 50 lbs. occasionally and move heavier objects with proper equipment. Exposure to typical manufacturing conditions (noise, moving equipment, and varying temperatures) should be expected; appropriate PPE is required in designated areas.

1. Basic Training and its component courses of Basic Fire Fighting, Elementary First Aid, Personal Safety and Social Responsibility, and Personal Survival Techniques. Approximately fifty (50) per year in total for basic training or component courses.

3. Advanced Fire Fighting. Approximately 20 training courses per year.

4. Operator of Uninspected Passenger Vessels. Approximately thirty (30) training courses per year.

5. Auxiliary Sail. Approximately ten (10) training courses per year.

6. Assistance Towing. Approximately fifteen (15) training courses per year.

7. Master 100. Approximately 35 training courses per year.

8. Master/Mate 200. Approximately fifteen (15) training courses per year.

9. Able Seaman, Rating Forming Part of a Navigation Watch, and Able Seafarer Deck. Approximately fifteen (15) training courses per year.

10. Radar and Automatic Radar plotting aids. Approximately 35 training courses per year

11. Maritime Security Awareness, Vessel Personnel with Designated Security Duties, Vessel Security Officer & 12 Company Security Officer and Facility Security Officer. Approximately 35 training courses per year.

12. Rules of the Road. Approximately ten (10) training courses per year.

13. Fast Rescue Boat.

14. Bridge Resource Management.

15. Proficiency in Survival Craft (including Limited, Refresher, Upgrade Limited to PSC).

16. Crowd Management.

title: Driving Instructor - CA
description:
Location: Richmond, CA


About us

Coastline Academy is the largest and fastest growing driving school in the country. Since 2017 we've taught more than 250,000 students across seven states, backed by over 100,000 five-star reviews. We're on a mission to eradicate car crashes by teaching safe and confident drivers for life. We're people-first and technology-centric: online booking, digital lesson reports, transparent pricing, modern cars. 98% of our students rate their lesson five stars.

Become part of a team committed to creating safe, confident drivers for life.


About this role

You'll sit in the passenger seat of a Coastline car and teach people something they'll use every day for the rest of their lives. Most of your students are teenagers taking their first turn behind the wheel. Some are adults getting ready for a road test. All of them leave your car more capable than when they got in.

  • You teach in our car, not yours. Every Coastline vehicle is company-provided, clearly marked, fitted with a second instructor brake, and inspected by certified mechanics.

Your training · 60 paid hours

  • 40 Hours Virtual Learning: Complete self-paced reading and interactive modules from home.
  • 20 Hours Hands-On Driving & Practical Mentorship: Shadow 10 hours live in-car lessons (five 2-hour lessons with students) and complete 10 hours of direct coaching with a Certified Trainer (two 5-hour sessions).


You'll never be conducting lessons alone in a car with a student until you're ready.


What you'll do

  • Teach the practical skills of driving, every aspect, from parking lots to freeway merges

  • Document and report on each student's progress
  • Stay in close, timely communication with your supervisor and support team
  • Bring professionalism to every interaction with students and teammates
  • Show up for team meetings, updates, and ongoing development

title: Adoption Specialist RPACS
description:
DePaul is seeking a Full-Time (37.5-hour workweek) Adoption Specialist in the Abingdon, VA location.

The Adoption Specialist (RPACS) will provide supportive services to adoptive families post-finalization to strengthen and maintain adoptive placements and prevent adoption disruption and dissolution. DePaul, in partnership with subcontractor Commonwealth Catholic Charities, offers a wide range of free support services to children and families once the goal of permanency is achieved. The Adoption Specialist for this program must understand the unique dynamics and challenges of families formed by adoption and then tailor support to the current needs of each family. Primary activities and responsibilities may include referrals and resource sharing, education and training for families, planning and facilitating family activities, planning and leadership of parent and youth discussion groups, and connecting families to adoption-competent clinical services. The Adoption Specialist (RPACS) provides support and crisis intervention when evolving family circumstances threaten adoption stability.

  • Perform strengths-based individualized intake, assess ongoing child and family strengths/needs post-adoption, and develop more detailed individualized service plans when warranted

  • Plan, coordinate, and facilitate adoptive family and child support groups, fun family activities, and opportunities for respite to enhance family connection with the broader adoptive community and natural supports
  • Prepare and maintain case records and reports according to program and grant standards concerning timeliness, content, accuracy, and confidentiality

Position Overview
Floor Interior Services (FIS) is seeking professional, dependable Measure Technicians to perform accurate in-home flooring measurements and deliver an exceptional customer experience.
This is an independent contractor opportunity. The Measure Technician will visit customers’ homes, evaluate project conditions, accurately measure all applicable areas, document project requirements, upload completed information, and provide the customer with an in-home installation quote.
This role is more than measuring rooms. The technician is often the customer’s first face-to-face interaction with our installation team and must represent FIS with professionalism, confidence, accuracy, and urgency.

Key Responsibilities
• Travel to scheduled customer appointments within the assigned service area.
• Contact customers before arrival and maintain professional communication regarding appointment timing.
• Arrive on time, professionally dressed, and prepared to complete the assignment.
• Accurately measure rooms, closets, stairs, transitions, doorways, and other applicable installation areas.
• Identify flooring types, subfloor conditions, transitions, furniture requirements, removal needs, installation challenges, and other project-specific details.
• Create accurate diagrams, room layouts, measurements, photographs, and supporting documentation.
• Ensure all required project information is complete before leaving the customer’s home.
• Upload measurements, diagrams, photographs, notes, and other required documentation within established timelines.
• Review the proposed installation scope with the customer and provide an accurate in-home quote using company-approved systems and pricing.
• Clearly explain the installation process, anticipated requirements, and next steps without making unauthorized promises.
• Answer customer questions professionally and help create confidence in moving forward with the project.
• Immediately report safety concerns, unusual site conditions, system issues, or potential scope problems.
• Protect customer information and maintain confidentiality.

Performance Expectations
Success in this role will be measured by:
• Measurement accuracy
• Quote accuracy and completeness
• On-time appointment arrival
• Timely data and documentation uploads
• Customer satisfaction
• Quote participation and conversion results
• Professional communication
• Low remeasure and correction rates
• Compliance with FIS and retail-partner requirements
Accuracy is non-negotiable. A rushed or incomplete measurement creates problems for the customer, installer, retailer, and company. Measure twice, upload once—the tape measure has no sympathy.

Required Qualifications
• Experience in flooring measurement, flooring installation, construction, estimating, in-home sales, or a related field is preferred.
• Strong mathematical, measuring, and spatial-reasoning skills.
• Ability to learn and accurately use electronic measuring and quoting systems.
• Comfortable presenting pricing and speaking directly with customers in their homes.
