This position is offered on an independent contractor basis. The contractor is responsible for their own transportation, equipment, insurance, taxes, business expenses, and compliance with applicable laws and contractual requirements.
Nothing in this description creates an employment relationship. Final expectations, compensation, service territory, scheduling requirements, performance standards, and contractor obligations will be governed by the applicable independent contractor agreement.

title: Associate Director, Translational Medicine - Clinical Biomarkers
description:
Position Title: Associate Director, Clinical Pharmacology

Job Status: Exempt, Full Time

Location: Remote

Department: Clinical Pharmacology


Company Overview

Enliven Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the discovery and development of small molecule inhibitors to help people with cancer not only live longer but live better. The Company aims to address existing and emerging unmet needs with a precision medicine approach that improves survival and enhances overall well-being. Its discovery process combines deep insights in clinically validated biological targets and differentiated chemistry with the goal of designing therapies

for unmet needs.


Position Summary

The Associate Director, Translational Medicine – Clinical Biomarkers, will lead the identification, evaluation, development, validation, and implementation of biomarker testing solutions supporting clinical development programs, with focus on chronic myeloid leukemia (CML).


This individual will develop clinical biomarker strategies, assess external laboratory and contract research organization (CRO) capabilities, and establish partnerships required to implement high-quality biomarker assays in clinical studies. The role will collaborate closely with Clinical Development, Translational Medicine, Clinical Operations, Regulatory Affairs, Data Management, Quality, and other cross-functional partners to support clinical study objectives and deliver long-term value across the research and development portfolio.


The successful candidate will have expertise in molecular biomarker assays for hematologic malignancies, including BCR::ABL1 mutation testing by next-generation sequencing (NGS) or Sanger sequencing for patient selection and BCR::ABL1 transcript quantification by qRT-PCR or digital PCR for efficacy and study-endpoint assessments.


Key Responsibilities

  • Lead the development and execution of clinical biomarker strategies for CML and other oncology programs.
  • Conduct landscape assessments and critically evaluate biomarker testing solutions offered by CROs and clinical laboratories, including BCR::ABL1 assays authorized, cleared, approved, or otherwise recognized by the FDA, EMA, or other applicable regulatory authorities.
  • Lead the development, transfer, optimization, qualification, and validation of biomarker assays for hematologic malignancies and other liquid-tumor applications.
  • Ensure that assay validation and implementation are appropriate for the assay’s intended use and clinical context
  • Establish and manage external laboratory partnerships, including project scope, timelines, deliverables, budgets, risks, change orders, and issue-resolution processes.
  • Evaluate biomarker data for accuracy, completeness, consistency, and biological plausibility, and identify potential assay-performance or sample-quality issues.
  • Partner with Clinical Development and Clinical Operations to review clinical protocols, laboratory manuals, informed-consent language, sample-collection schedules, biomarker analysis plans, and study reports.
  • Collaborate with Regulatory Affairs on biomarker and companion diagnostic strategies, regulatory submissions, briefing packages, health-authority questions, and interactions with the FDA, EMA, and other regulatory authorities.
  • Provide expertise on current regulatory expectations for exploratory biomarkers, clinical trial assays, investigational device exemption requirements, companion diagnostics, laboratory-developed tests, and in vitro diagnostic development
  • Work with Quality Assurance to qualify biomarker CROs and laboratories and support periodic or risk-based vendor audits. Ensure timely resolution of audit findings and implementation of corrective and preventive actions.
  • Review vendor invoices against contracts, statements of work, completed activities, and agreed deliverables as part of effective vendor and budget management.

All responsibilities are carried out in accordance with the established policies and procedures of the dialysis center.

Qualifications:

  1. High school diploma or equivalent — Required

  2. Current Basic Life Support (BLS) certification from the American Heart Association — Required

  3. Certified Hemodialysis Technician through:

    • Board of Nephrology Examiners Nursing and Technology (BONENT) or

    • National Association of Nephrology Technicians/Technologists (NANT) — Required

  1. Perform routine dialysis procedures, including:

    • Initiation and termination of treatments

  3. Conduct and document pre-dialysis safety tests accurately.

  4. Monitor and record:

    • Blood flow rates

    • Machine pressures

    • Heparin dosages

  9. Monitor patient status throughout treatment and immediately report any abnormal signs or symptoms to the nurse.

  10. Obtain and properly label blood specimens; complete laboratory requisitions.

  11. Spin blood specimens in a centrifuge, as required.

  12. Complete all required documentation accurately and report any unusual events to the supervisor.

Position Overview
Floor Interior Services (FIS) is seeking professional, dependable Measure Technicians to perform accurate in-home flooring measurements and deliver an exceptional customer experience.
This is an independent contractor opportunity. The Measure Technician will visit customers’ homes, evaluate project conditions, accurately measure all applicable areas, document project requirements, upload completed information, and provide the customer with an in-home installation quote.
This role is more than measuring rooms. The technician is often the customer’s first face-to-face interaction with our installation team and must represent FIS with professionalism, confidence, accuracy, and urgency.

Key Responsibilities
• Travel to scheduled customer appointments within the assigned service area.
• Contact customers before arrival and maintain professional communication regarding appointment timing.

• Identify flooring types, subfloor conditions, transitions, furniture requirements, removal needs, installation challenges, and other project-specific details.
• Create accurate diagrams, room layouts, measurements, photographs, and supporting documentation.
• Ensure all required project information is complete before leaving the customer’s home.
• Upload measurements, diagrams, photographs, notes, and other required documentation within established timelines.
• Review the proposed installation scope with the customer and provide an accurate in-home quote using company-approved systems and pricing.

• Answer customer questions professionally and help create confidence in moving forward with the project.
• Immediately report safety concerns, unusual site conditions, system issues, or potential scope problems.


Required Qualifications
• Experience in flooring measurement, flooring installation, construction, estimating, in-home sales, or a related field is preferred.
• Strong mathematical, measuring, and spatial-reasoning skills.
• Ability to learn and accurately use electronic measuring and quoting systems.
• Comfortable presenting pricing and speaking directly with customers in their homes.
• Strong attention to detail and commitment to completing documentation correctly.
• Professional appearance, communication, and customer-service skills.
• Dependable transportation and willingness to travel throughout the assigned territory.
• Smartphone, tablet, or other required technology capable of running company-approved applications.
• Ability to work independently, manage appointments, and meet established deadlines.

Physical Requirements

• Ability to safely access rooms, closets, stairs, exterior areas, and other project spaces.

This position is offered on an independent contractor basis. The contractor is responsible for their own transportation, equipment, insurance, taxes, business expenses, and compliance with applicable laws and contractual requirements.

title: Intern-HR Documentation Assistant (Tripoli- Benghazi)
description:

Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. This includes proper labeling, categorization, updating databases, responding to document requests, and performing regular audits of archived information. The intern will also assist in administrative and clerical tasks to support HR operations.

3. Required competencies


  • Basic computer literacy and proficiency in Microsoft Office applications.

  • Strong attention to detail and accuracy.
  • Ability to handle confidential information with discretion and professionalism.
  • Ability to work collaboratively, take instructions, and seek clarification when needed.

4. Key Responsibilities

  • Assist in archiving HR documents and employee records in compliance with IRC policies and legal requirements.

  • Ensure accurate labelling, categorization and indexing of files for easy retrieval.
  • Support in maintaining confidentiality and security of personnel files and sensitive information.
  • Help update and maintain the HR database and file tracking systems.
  • Conduct periodic audits of archived documents to ensure completeness and accuracy.
  • Provide support in responding to internal document retrieval requests.
  • Collaborate with the HR team to streamline filing and recordkeeping processes.
  • Perform other administrative and clerical tasks as assigned.

5. Conditions

  • Work for 8 hours a day from 9:00 – 17:00 Sunday to Thursday.
  • Accuracy and flexibility are required in timing.

6. Duration of Contract: 2 Months

7. Expected Deliverables

• Physical office documents reviewed and prepared for archiving.

• All assigned documents scanned and saved electronically.

• Electronic files properly named and organized within the designated folder structure.

• Progress tracker updated regularly throughout the assignment.

• Completion of the digitization and archiving activities assigned during the internship period.

Professional Standards: All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. Change, Readiness and Adoption

Governance, Compliance and Vendor Management

  • Proven ability to manage project scope, timelines, budgets, resources, risks, dependencies, and vendors.
  • Experience working in a matrix organisation and partnering with regional or global technology teams.

Core Competencies

  • Portfolio and project management
  • Business analysis and requirements management
  • Change management and user adoption
  • Communication, facilitation, and influencing
  • Risk, issue, and dependency management

Key Stakeholders

Internal: Market Business Leadership, Market TECH & Digital Solutions, Regional TECH & Digital Solutions, product owners, Finance, Risk, Cybersecurity, Legal and Data Privacy teams.


External: Technology vendors, system integrators, consultants, and implementation partners.

title: Gender, Protection and Empowerment Coordinator
description:
Program Leadership and Coordination

  • Coordinate with program teams and sectors to mainstream gender and protection throughout project design, implementation, and evaluation processes.
  • To effectively implement gender and protection strategies across all regions, the Coordinator will liaise with field focal points or designated program staff in each location, where available, and advocate for dedicated support where needed.
  • Act as the Country Office focal point for the Gender Action Plan (GAP), leading its development, implementation, monitoring, and reporting.

PSEA and Safeguarding Focal Point Duties

    • Serve as the PSEA Focal Point for NPA Syria, ensuring alignment with global safeguarding standards.
    • Provide training and awareness sessions on PSEA to staff and partners.
    • Support the development of reporting and response mechanisms for protection violations in coordination with senior management.

Gender and Protection Mainstreaming

    • Ensure that all NPA Syria programs and activities are planned and executed with an inclusive gender and protection lens.
    • Develop, implement, and maintain practical guidance for gender and protection mainstreaming.
    • Embed gender and protection indicators into project-level and organizational M&E frameworks.

Cross-Sectoral Support

    • Provide technical gender and protection support to all NPA Syria programs, including:
      • Humanitarian relief efforts (e.g., emergency responses, displaced population services)
      • Development programming (e.g., livelihoods, education, capacity building)
      • Civil society strengthening and partner support
      • Mine Action and Risk Education operations, in collaboration with the Mine Action team
      • Liaise with Global Gender and Protection Advisors to ensure strategic coherence.

Assessments, Audits, and Tool Development

      • Lead gender and protection assessments and risk analyses across programs and offices.
      • Develop, adapt, and implement culturally appropriate tools and methodologies for data collection and analysis.
      • Conduct periodic gender audits and use findings to recommend actionable improvements.

Capacity Development

      • Assess partner and staff capacity in gender and protection.
      • Design and deliver training, mentoring, and guidance tailored to field realities and program types.
      • Provide direct technical support to implementing partners to enhance their integration of gender and protection in programming.

Documentation, Reporting, and Learning

      • Lead documentation of gender, protection, and empowerment outcomes and impact across all sectors.
      • Ensure timely, high-quality donor and internal reporting on gender and protection indicators.
      • Document lessons learned, best practices, and success stories.

Advocacy and Representation

      • Represent NPA Syria in national coordination forums and sector working groups on Gender, Protection, and PSEA.
      • Advocate for the inclusion of gender and protection perspectives in sectoral and cross-sectoral strategies.
      • Build and maintain relationships with national stakeholders, including women-led organizations, authorities, and donors

l . Perform routine treatment procedures such as insertion of fistula needles, initiation, and termination of treatments.

title: Driving Instructor - CA
description:
CLICK THE CITY & STATE ABOVE TO VIEW OUR EXACT LOCATION


About us

Coastline Academy is the largest and fastest growing driving school in the country. Since 2017 we've taught more than 250,000 students across seven states, backed by over 100,000 five-star reviews. We're on a mission to eradicate car crashes by teaching safe and confident drivers for life. We're people-first and technology-centric: online booking, digital lesson reports, transparent pricing, modern cars. 98% of our students rate their lesson five stars.

Become part of a team committed to creating safe, confident drivers for life.


About this role

You'll sit in the passenger seat of a Coastline car and teach people something they'll use every day for the rest of their lives. Most of your students are teenagers taking their first turn behind the wheel. Some are adults getting ready for a road test. All of them leave your car more capable than when they got in.

  • You teach in our car, not yours. Every Coastline vehicle is company-provided, clearly marked, fitted with a second instructor brake, and inspected by certified mechanics.
  • We pay for your certification. Our training team walks you through your state's driving instructor licensing requirements and provides the coursework. Training is paid.
  • Every lesson is recorded. Dashcams capture video and audio inside and outside the car for your safety and your student's.
  • Your schedule follows the students. Most of our students are in school, so demand concentrates in afternoons and weekends. A typical day is three two-hour lessons.


Your training · 60 paid hours

  • 40 Hours Virtual Learning: Complete self-paced reading and interactive modules from home.
  • 20 Hours Hands-On Driving & Practical Mentorship: Shadow 10 hours live in-car lessons (five 2-hour lessons with students) and complete 10 hours of direct coaching with a Certified Trainer (two 5-hour sessions).


You'll never be conducting lessons alone in a car with a student until you're ready.


What you'll do

  • Teach the practical skills of driving, every aspect, from parking lots to freeway merges
  • Coach students on the rules of the road
  • Build confidence, not just competence
  • Take control of the vehicle when a situation calls for it
  • Document and report on each student's progress
  • Stay in close, timely communication with your supervisor and support team
  • Bring professionalism to every interaction with students and teammates
  • Show up for team meetings, updates, and ongoing development

Job Title: Instructional Coach
Classification: Non-Exempt; Full-time
Supervisor: Education Manager
Pay Grade: Grade 11; step depending on experience and qualifications
Schedule: Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m.-5:00p.m.; 12 Month Employee. hours may vary based on program needs.

Position Summary
The Instructional Coach provides individualized, practice-based coaching and instructional support to Head Start and Early Head Start teaching staff to strengthen effective teaching practices, responsive caregiving, classroom environments, child engagement, and positive adult-child interactions for infants, toddlers, and preschool-aged children. This position supports teaching staff in applying developmentally appropriate and evidence-based practices aligned with the Head Start Early Learning Outcomes Framework.

The Instructional Coach works collaboratively with teachers, Teacher Assistants, Education Managers, Site Managers, and other program staff to support professional growth and classroom quality. The position conducts classroom observations, provides reflection and feedback, assists with the implementation of effective instructional practices, and uses coaching and observation information to support continuous improvement. Coaching is provided through the Practice-Based Coaching model, including shared goals, action planning, focused observation, reflection, feedback, and follow-up.
Connection to EOAC's Work
Vision: Every family thriving.
Mission: EOAC moves families forward by connecting them to opportunities that build lasting stability.
Every EOAC position contributes to the agency’s mission, values, and strategic plan. The Instructional Coach supports EOAC’s work by helping teaching staff strengthen classroom practices and provide high-quality learning and caregiving experiences that promote positive outcomes for children and families.
· Putting people first by supporting practices that promote children’s safety, development, learning, engagement, and well-being while building respectful and supportive relationships with teaching staff.
· Acting with integrity by providing objective feedback, maintaining confidentiality, completing accurate documentation, and following Head Start, licensing, and EOAC requirements.
· Working together by developing collaborative coaching relationships with teaching staff and partnering with Education leadership and program staff to address classroom needs.
· Focusing on results by establishing meaningful coaching goals, using observation and assessment information, monitoring progress, and supporting improvements in teaching practices and classroom quality.

Key Outcomes
· Teaching staff receive consistent, individualized, and meaningful instructional coaching that supports professional growth.
· Coaching goals and action plans are clearly established, documented, monitored, and followed through.
· Classroom observations and quality-assessment activities identify strengths, areas for improvement, and opportunities for additional support.
· Teaching staff receive timely, specific, objective, and constructive feedback that supports improved classroom practice.
· Developmentally appropriate, evidence-based, culturally responsive, and linguistically responsive teaching and caregiving practices are supported and implemented.
· Required CLASS, QCIT, Classroom Environmental Checklist, Frog Street Fidelity, and other assigned observation activities are completed accurately and on time.
· Coaching documentation, ChildPlus records, Coaching Logs, Weekly Schedules, and other required records are accurate, timely, and complete.
· Coaching information and classroom trends are used to support professional development, Continuous Quality Improvement, classroom quality, and positive outcomes for children.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Instructional Coaching
· Provide individualized instructional coaching to assigned Head Start and Early Head Start teachers and Teacher Assistants using the Practice-Based Coaching model.
· Establish collaborative coaching relationships that promote trust, reflection, professional growth, and accountability.
· Develop shared coaching goals and individualized action plans based on identified needs and aligned with program goals, school readiness goals, curricula, and professional development priorities.
· Conduct coaching cycles that include focused observation, reflection, feedback, practice, and follow-up.
· Provide timely, specific, objective, and constructive feedback regarding teaching and caregiving practices.
· Facilitate reflective conversations that help teaching staff examine and strengthen their classroom practices.
· Model effective instructional, caregiving, child engagement, classroom management, and behavior-support practices as appropriate.
· Provide technical assistance to support the implementation of developmentally appropriate and evidence-based practices.
· Assist teaching staff in applying professional development and training to daily classroom practice.
· Identify professional development needs through coaching, observations, assessments, monitoring results, and teacher input.
Classroom Observation and Quality Assessment
· Conduct scheduled and informal classroom observations to support coaching and classroom quality.
· Complete required Classroom Environmental Checklists two times per year.
· Complete Formal CLASS Observations for Head Start two times per year as assigned.
· Conduct Informal CLASS observations as needed.
· Complete required QCIT observations for Early Head Start two times per year.
· Complete the Frog Street Fidelity Tool during Formal Observations as required.
· Use observation and assessment information to identify strengths, coaching priorities, and areas requiring additional support.
· Communicate significant classroom, safety, compliance, or performance concerns to the appropriate Education leadership.
· Keep coaching focused on helping staff improve their classroom practices and separate from supervision or disciplinary action.

Teaching and Child Development Support
· Support teaching staff in implementing developmentally appropriate practices for infants, toddlers, and preschool-aged children.
· Promote responsive caregiving, positive adult-child interactions, child engagement, and effective learning environments.
· Support instructional practices that promote children’s language, cognitive, social-emotional, physical, and overall development.
· Support culturally and linguistically responsive teaching and caregiving practices.
· Support strategies that respond to individual children’s developmental and learning needs, including children with disabilities or developmental delays.
· Reinforce practices aligned with the Head Start Early Learning Outcomes Framework and approved program curricula.
· Promote developmentally appropriate approaches to behavior guidance and positive social-emotional development.

Documentation and Compliance
· Document coaching activities, observations, goals, action plans, feedback, follow-up, and progress in ChildPlus.
· Maintain accurate Coaching Logs and other required coaching records.
· Submit the Weekly Schedule to the Education Manager each Friday in accordance with program procedures.
· Complete required ChildPlus documentation by the end of each workday.
· Maintain complete and accurate records to support program monitoring, reporting, audits, and Continuous Quality Improvement.
· Maintain confidentiality regarding children, families, employees, personnel matters, and program information.
· Support compliance with Head Start Program Performance Standards, the Head Start Early Learning Outcomes Framework, Texas Child Care Licensing requirements, and EOAC policies and procedures.
· Report documentation, compliance, safety, or procedural concerns to the appropriate Education leadership.

Collaboration and Continuous Quality Improvement
· Review coaching, observation, assessment, and classroom-quality information to identify trends and areas of opportunity.
· Communicate relevant coaching trends, classroom needs, and professional development opportunities to Education Managers and program leadership.
· Communicate regularly with the Education Manager, Assistant Director of Program Services, and other appropriate staff about coaching needs, trends, and progress toward program goals.
· Participate in Continuous Quality Improvement activities related to classroom quality, instructional practices, teacher development, and child outcomes.
· Assist with implementation of approved instructional strategies, curriculum practices, professional development initiatives, and program improvements.
· Collaborate with Education Managers, Site Managers, teachers, Teacher Assistants, and other program staff to strengthen classroom quality.
· Participate in staff meetings, professional development activities, planning sessions, and other program activities as assigned.
Core Competencies
· Practice-Based Coaching: Uses coaching strategies that promote reflection, professional growth, accountability, and improvement.
· Early Childhood Practice: Applies sound early childhood practices to support effective teaching, responsive caregiving, and child development.
· Observation and Feedback: Conducts objective observations and provides clear, specific, and constructive feedback.
· Communication and Relationship Building: Builds respectful, collaborative relationships and communicates effectively with teaching staff and leadership.
· Organization and Follow-Through: Manages coaching assignments, observations, documentation, schedules, and deadlines accurately and consistently.
· Professional Judgment: Recognizes concerns, maintains appropriate professional boundaries, and communicates matters requiring additional guidance or management attention.
· Continuous Improvement: Uses observation, data, reflection, and feedback to identify opportunities for improvement and support progress.
· Professionalism and Confidentiality: Maintains confidentiality, objectivity, ethical conduct, and professionalism in all interactions.

Knowledge and Skills
· Knowledge of infant, toddler, and preschool child development and developmentally appropriate early childhood practices.
· Understanding of responsive caregiving, positive adult-child interactions, child engagement, social-emotional development, and effective classroom environments.
· Knowledge of Head Start and Early Head Start program requirements, the Head Start Early Learning Outcomes Framework, and applicable Texas Child Care Licensing requirements.
· Understanding of Practice-Based Coaching principles and effective instructional and professional development practices.
· Knowledge of adult learning principles and effective coaching strategies.
· Ability to use observations, assessments, and program data to identify coaching needs and support program and school readiness goals.
· Ability to observe classroom practices, identify strengths and areas for improvement, provide constructive feedback, and support implementation of effective teaching practices.
· Strong communication, interpersonal, organizational, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage multiple assignments and maintain accurate documentation.
· Strong computer skills, including Microsoft Office, ChildPlus, electronic documentation systems, data collection tools, and technology used for communication and reporting.
· Ability to maintain confidentiality, exercise sound professional judgment, and work collaboratively with teaching staff, Education leadership, and other program staff.

Qualifications
· Bachelor’s degree in Early Childhood Education, Child Development, Early Childhood Special Education, Human Development, or a closely related field.
· Minimum of two years of professional experience working with infants, toddlers, and/or preschool-aged children in an early childhood setting.
· Must successfully complete all required pre-employment requirements, including applicable background checks and pre-employment drug screening.
· Must possess and maintain a valid driver’s license.
· Must be able to travel between EOAC locations as required to perform job duties and attend required meetings, trainings, conferences, or other program-related activities.

Preferred Qualifications
· Experience working in a Head Start or Early Head Start program.
· Experience providing coaching, mentoring, technical assistance, or professional development to early childhood staff.
· Experience conducting classroom observations and providing professional feedback.
· Experience using the Practice-Based Coaching model or a similar coaching approach.
· Experience with CLASS, QCIT, Frog Street Fidelity, or similar classroom observation and quality-assessment tools.
· Training or experience in adult learning principles and the use of assessment data to guide individualized coaching.

Physical Demands and Work Environment
· Ability to sit, stand, walk, bend, stoop, kneel, and work at floor level for periods of time while observing and supporting classroom activities.
· Ability to lift, carry, push, or pull materials and equipment weighing up to 30 pounds occasionally.
· Ability to safely navigate active classroom, playground, and other program environments.
· Ability to maintain visual and auditory awareness of children, staff, and classroom activities.
· Regular exposure to classroom noise, active movement, cleaning and classroom materials, outdoor conditions, and communicable illnesses commonly associated with early childhood settings.

Other Duties
This job description is not intended to list every duty, responsibility, or qualification associated with the position. The Instructional Coach may be assigned additional duties by the Education Manager or program leadership as needed to support Head Start operations and EOAC’s mission.

Drone Systems Engineer

Location: Lafayette, LA
Position Type: Full-Time

About DMR Technologies

DMR Technologies designs and manufactures advanced unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) supporting agriculture, public safety, critical infrastructure, and defense. Our products combine mechanical engineering, electrical systems, embedded electronics, software, manufacturing, and autonomous technologies into complete drone platforms built in the United States. We’re seeking a Drone Systems Engineer who enjoys building products, solving technical challenges, and working across engineering disciplines to deliver reliable systems from concept through production.

Position Summary

The Drone Systems Engineer serves as the bridge between mechanical, electrical, software, manufacturing, and flight operations teams. This role is responsible for integrating subsystems into complete aircraft, validating performance, solving technical issues, and continuously improving DMR's products throughout their lifecycle. This position is ideal for engineers who enjoy hands-on product development and are energized by seeing their work deployed in real-world environments.

Responsibilities

  • Integrate mechanical, electrical, software, and communications systems into complete drone platforms
  • Build, troubleshoot, and validate engineering prototypes
  • Plan and execute laboratory and flight testing
  • Analyze test data and recommend design improvements
  • Support payload integration, avionics, sensors, and communication systems
  • Create and maintain engineering documentation, Bills of Material, and assembly procedures
  • Collaborate with manufacturing to improve product quality and production efficiency
  • Support root cause investigations and corrective actions
  • Participate in customer demonstrations and field evaluations as needed
  • Mentor engineering interns and support junior technical staff
  • Evaluate emerging technologies that improve DMR products and engineering processes
Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Computer Engineering, Robotics, Mechatronics, or a related field
  • 3–6 years of engineering experience involving robotics, UAVs, aerospace, industrial automation, or electromechanical products
  • Strong troubleshooting and analytical skills
  • Excellent communication and cross-functional collaboration abilities
  • Comfortable working in both office and production environments
Preferred Technical Experience

Experience with several of the following:

  • SolidWorks or equivalent CAD software
  • UAV flight controllers and avionics
  • Electrical integration and wiring
  • Sensor and payload integration
  • Battery and power systems
  • Manufacturing and Design for Manufacturing (DFM)
  • Python, JavaScript, or scripting languages
  • Git and engineering documentation tools
  • AI-assisted engineering and development tools
  • FAA Part 107 Remote Pilot Certificate (preferred)
What Success Looks Like

Successful Drone Systems Engineers think beyond individual components and understand how complete systems work together. They are comfortable reviewing CAD models, troubleshooting hardware, supporting manufacturing, participating in flight tests, and collaborating with software developers to solve integration challenges. They are builders, problem solvers, and continuous learners who enjoy seeing products move rapidly from concept to customer deployment.

Why Join DMR?

At DMR, you'll have the opportunity to influence products from the earliest design stages through production and customer deployment. Rather than working on a single subsystem, you'll collaborate across engineering disciplines while helping develop the next generation of American-made unmanned aircraft systems.

or

title: Automotive Lube Tech
description:
We're growing and we'd love to have you grow with us

Atlantic Coast Enterprises is seeking to hire part-time and full-time Automotive Technicians to provide top-notch service at a Jiffy Lube in St. Petersburg, FL. Are you looking to learn and advance your skills with a company that cares about its employees? Do you want to work in a collaborative, positive environment where humor, teamwork, and laughter are encouraged? If so, keep reading!

Our Automotive Technicians/Auto Mechanics earn a salary of up to $40,000 per year based on experience. We also offer generous benefits including paid vacation after one year of employment, longevity bonuses, comprehensive health care, dental/vision insurance, basic life insurance, short-term disability, long-term disability, a 401(k) plan, bereavement leave, and employee oil changes and discounts. If this sounds like the right part-time or full-time position for you, apply today!

ABOUT ATLANTIC COAST ENTERPRISES

Atlantic Coast Enterprises (ACE) is a full-service lubrication, fluid, and automotive maintenance center. We offer our customers these services in the cleanest, most professional surroundings possible. Each day we strive to achieve our mission to create customers for life through fast, friendly, clean, and professional service. We are dedicated to expanding and moving constantly on to new and different challenges. A few short years ago, we were recognized as the franchisee of the year within the Jiffy Lube nationwide network.

Everything at ACE is a team effort. We know that without our employees we wouldn't be able to grow, improve, or create lifelong customers. This is why we offer competitive compensation, generous benefits, and a supportive, collaborative environment. We encourage each and every employee to share their ideas with us.

A DAY IN THE LIFE OF A LUBE TECH

You arrive each day determined to take excellent care of our customers. They trust your competence, as well as your integrity to keep their vehicles running. Utilizing the training we have provided, you are able to correctly identify mechanical problems, provide preventative maintenance, and carefully address customer concerns. With your excellent communication skills, you give recommendations for repairs along with proper labor and time estimates. You then make the repairs and replace parts as requested. Your positive attitude and ability to stay on top of the latest knowledge and training ensure your success!

QUALIFICATIONS

  • At least 18 years old
  • Valid driver's license
  • Physical ability to perform typical tasks required for repairing and servicing vehicles including the ability to stand for several hours at a time and lift up to 50 lbs
  • Comfortable working in a variety of weather conditions

No experience? Don't worry! We will teach you everything you need to know. Any previous experience is a plus! Do you have excellent mechanical skills and the drive to problem-solve? Are you able to work independently and in a team environment? Do you have exceptional customer service skills? If so, you may be perfect for this part-time or full-time position!

WORK SCHEDULE

Our Lube Techs work anywhere from 15-40 hours/week depending on part-time or full-time status. The typical work schedule varies during our business hours and will include a mix of day, evening, and weekend shifts--but no late nights. We are open 8am to 7pm Monday-Saturday and 9am to 4pm on Sunday.

ARE YOU READY TO JOIN OUR TEAM?

If you feel that you are right for this position, apply now with our initial 3-minute, mobile-friendly application.

title: Senior Cloud System Engineer
description:

title: Adoption Specialist RPACS
description:
DePaul is seeking a Full-Time (37.5 hour workweek) Adoption Specialist in the Lynchburg, VA location.

JOB SUMMARY:
The Adoption Specialist (RPACS) will provide supportive services to adoptive families post-finalization to strengthen and maintain adoptive placements and prevent adoption disruption and dissolution. DePaul, in partnership with subcontractor Commonwealth Catholic Charities, offers a wide range of free support services to children and families once the goal of permanency is achieved. The Adoption Specialist for this program must understand the unique dynamics and challenges of families formed by adoption and then tailor support to the current needs of each family. Primary activities and responsibilities may include referrals and resource sharing, education and training for families, planning and facilitating family activities, planning and leadership of parent and youth discussion groups, and connecting families to adoption-competent clinical services. The Adoption Specialist (RPACS) provides support and crisis intervention when evolving family circumstances threaten adoption stability.
SUPERVISION RECEIVED AND EXERCISED:
The Adoption Specialist (RPACS) will report directly to the RPACS Regional Adoption Supervisor.
ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS AND DUTIES:
This list is not an exhaustive & all-inclusive list of job responsibilities. The distribution of time allotted for any function or duty is subject to change with or without notice. Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign other responsibilities to this job or reassign them elsewhere at any time.
  • Perform strengths-based individualized intake, assess ongoing child and family strengths/needs post-adoption, and develop more detailed individualized service plans when warranted
  • Provide families with specialized services that address core adoption issues, including information and referral, education, support, crisis management, and advocacy
  • Plan, coordinate, and facilitate adoptive family and child support groups, fun family activities, and opportunities for respite to enhance family connection with the broader adoptive community and natural supports
  • Prepare and maintain case records and reports according to program and grant standards concerning timeliness, content, accuracy, and confidentiality
  • Collaborate with supervisor, adoption team members, other DePaul staff across programs, and community partners to optimize services and program outcomes
  • Serve on multi-agency groups or deliver occasional adoption competence education to the community to enhance community-wide support of adoptive families
  • Complete other duties as assigned
KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, ABILITIES & OTHER CHARACTERISTICS REQUIRED:
Knowledge, skills, abilities, and other characteristics or KSAOs are attributes needed to perform a job that are demonstrated through qualifying training, education, and experience. This list is not an exhaustive & all-inclusive list of all KSAOs for this job.
Knowledge of:
  • Office and records administration techniques and procedures
  • The structure and content of the English language, including the meaning and spelling of words, rules of composition, and grammar
  • Microsoft Office Word, Excel, Powerpoint, Outlook, Sharepoint, Teams, and virtual meeting applications such as Zoom, WebEx, Google Meet
  • DePaul's policies, procedures, and standard practices and the rules and guidelines established by regulatory and governing agencies
  • Relevant policies, procedures, and strategies to promote the safety and protection of people, data, and property
  • Office procedures and spelling, grammar, punctuation, and arithmetic
  • Policies, procedures, and guidelines established by DePaul, professional organizations, governing agencies, and local laws, statutes, regulations, codes, and standards related to the area of responsibility
  • Motor vehicle operations, traffic rules and regulations, and maintenance of motor vehicles
Skill/Ability to:
  • Demonstrate interpersonal and verbal skills to defuse emotional situations, calm upset individuals, allay fears, and lessen confusion.
  • Give full attention to what other people are saying, take time to understand the points being made, ask questions as appropriate, and not interrupt at inappropriate times
  • Demonstrate verbal and written communication and body language that purveys professional composure, emotional intelligence, thoughtfulness, patience, and respect amidst change, ambiguity, and within the daily trajectories of work
  • Operate standard office equipment such as telephone, calculator, printer, scanner, cellular phone, tablet, computer, postage machine, shredder
  • Collect and analyze data
  • Manage multiple priorities and complete assignments on time, accurately, and with attention to detail, and ensure a high-quality work product
  • Develop and maintain professional working relationships and appropriate boundaries with individuals served, coworkers, management, community partners, and business associates, and work collaboratively in a team environment
  • Operate a computer and utilize computer applications, including spreadsheets, databases, word processing, email, internet, virtual meetings, internet, and department or program-specific software
  • Develop objectives, evaluate effectiveness, and assess service plans for individuals served
  • Analyze and prepare concise and accurate documents, reports, and correspondence
  • Communicate effectively in both oral and written form
  • Read and understand information and ideas presented in writing
  • Make arithmetical computations and tabulations
  • Effectively communicate policies and procedures clearly and concisely to coworkers, providers, and community partners
  • Effectively market the programs and services of the department and organization
  • Exercise sound judgment and critical thinking in decision-making and solving various work-related situations
  • Learn and adhere to policies, procedures, and guidelines established by DePaul, professional organizations, governing agencies, and local laws, statutes, regulations, codes, and standards related to the area of responsibility
  • Assist with the general upkeep and cleaning of office areas and agency vehicles
Other Characteristics:
  • Demonstrate self-awareness, ongoing self-evaluation, and a commitment to being part of a diverse, equitable, respectful, and inclusive workplace where all people are valued
  • Demonstrate professional composure in difficult and stressful situations
  • Demonstrate the FIRST (fairness, integrity, respect, safety, trust) values in the daily trajectories of work
  • Demonstrate professionalism regarding access to sensitive and confidential information related to employees, clients, and business records with no disclosure to others without needing to know
MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS TO APPLY:
A Bachelor's degree in social work or a related human services field with one year of experience providing casework services to children or families is required. Experience as a foster/adoptive parent could substitute for formal casework experience. Individuals possessing the required education yet lacking the necessary experience may be hired as a Trainee.
WORK ENVIRONMENT:
The work environment characteristics described herein represent those an employee encounters while performing the position's essential functions. The employee regularly works in an office environment and occasionally in the field. Due to the nature of the work, the incumbent may be exposed to situations of a highly emotional nature; incumbents are expected to use verbal skills to resolve interpersonal situations to achieve desired results independently. Incumbents are exposed to various living situations and lifestyles. Work is generally completed regularly during weekdays; however, daily work hours may vary. Participation in and completion of job duties outside of normally scheduled hours may be required. Work is subject to frequent interruptions, and noise levels are varied based on the work locations.
PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:
The physical demands described herein are representative of those that an employee in this position must meet, with or without reasonable accommodations, to perform the essential functions successfully. Physical activities required are finger dexterity necessary to operate equipment used in the position, effective communication and seeing or hearing verbal cues. Walking from one-third to two-thirds of the time, sitting from one-third to two-thirds of the time, standing from one-third to two-thirds of the time, bending from one-third to two-thirds of the time, stooping up to one-third of the time, lifting/pushing/pulling no more than twenty pounds is required. When accessing various locations, the incumbent must climb stairs and ramps. This position requires driving approximately fifteen percent of the employee's working time to various locations. Public transportation may not be available. Individuals needing reasonable accommodations should speak with their immediate supervisor/hiring manager.
SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS AND QUALIFICATIONS:
After a conditional job offer, the following may be required: current DMV driving record with results that comply with insurer guidelines; drug and alcohol screening with satisfactory results stipulated by applicable governing, funding, or regulatory agencies; criminal and child protective services background report. The applicant shall not have been convicted of any barrier crime(s) on the criminal background report. The applicant will have no founded disposition of child abuse or neglect as documented by the Child Protective Services background report.

DePaul is an Equal Opportunity Employer and E-Verify participant.

Flexible work from home options available.

Job Title: Volunteer Coordinator
Reports to: Director of Visitor Services
Department: Visitor Services
Position Status: Full-Time, exempt
Salary: $50,000 - $60,000
Position Description:
The Esplanade Association (EA) is honored to be a premier location for volunteerism in the Boston area, hosting more than 1,000 volunteers annually to build community in and care for the Charles River Esplanade. EA is seeking a Volunteer Coordinator to oversee a comprehensive individual and group volunteer program, and to effectively steward both in-kind and revenue-generating volunteer participation. Working closely with the Visitor Services and Horticulture departments, this position will organize, market, and staff volunteer activities year-round. In addition to care for the park and its visitors, the Volunteer Coordinator will maintain and maximize relationships built around volunteer activities to encourage further support for the park.
Responsibilities:
Volunteer Program (90%)
Volunteer Ambassador Program for Individuals—
  • Shepherd a robust network of Volunteer Ambassadors in daily volunteer roles, including the application process, training, and regular learning and social opportunities that reinforce a high-quality volunteer community.
  • Support daily volunteer work at the Charlesbank Campus info desk as well as at programs and events.
  • Ensure volunteer participation meets our standards. Address individual volunteer performance as needed.
  • Send regular Volunteer Ambassador updates and maintain Volunteer Ambassador relationships.
  • Generate and communicate about a regular Volunteer Ambassador schedule using an online platform.
  • Assess and improve the Volunteer Ambassador program and volunteer appreciation strategies.
  • Develop a recruitment plan for individual volunteers. Conduct outreach, promote opportunities, and increase access to application(s).
Group Volunteer Program—
  • Actively oversee group volunteer events, on average 2 per week, in multiple spaces throughout the park.
  • Organize and communicate the accurate scheduling of group volunteer events including date and time, project(s) to be completed, and group size.
  • Lead major community park service events, including EA’s annual joint-organizational Annual Charles River Cleanup as part of the Department of Conservation and Recreation’s Park Serve Day in observance of Earth Day.
  • Maintain and update the database of corporate and non-profit group volunteer contacts. Regularly share contacts with department head and Development team to cultivate deeper relationships.
  • Collaborate across departments to determine and select the best group projects based on seasonal park needs.
  • Maintain an inventory of volunteer tools, equipment, and safety supplies that are ready for each group.
  • Promote the benefits of further participation/support of EA programs and projects.
Accounting—
  • With direction from the department head, create and maintain the annual volunteer program budget, including giving input on revenue goals and expense limits.
  • Benchmark corporate group rates annually and consistently hone strategies to grow revenue.
  • Manage invoicing and secure owed or past-due donation payments.
Marketing and Reporting—
  • With the support of Marketing staff, draft compelling marketing materials and maintain volunteer webpages to drive participation in the volunteer programs, with special emphasis on the annual launch of activities.
  • Research prospective corporate volunteer groups for online outreach.
  • Photograph groups and calculate volunteer impacts. Enhance acknowledgements for contributions if possible.
  • Translate annual volunteer data into useful metrics to communicate program impact year-over-year.
Visitor Services Support (10%)
  • Actively support superior visitor experience in all aspects of work including frequent conversations, wayfinding help, and inquiry response in the park and at the Charlesbank Campus info desk. Provide support to volunteers as they accomplish these tasks.
  • Work closely with other staff to develop a familiarity with programs and events that occur on Charlesbank Campus and in the park.
  • Provide secondary support to other members of the Visitor Services team, especially as it relates to volunteer duties and public outreach.
  • Advance creative ideas and pilot new initiatives for volunteer support.
  • Support periodic EA-focused fundraising events and activities.
  • Perform other duties as directed or as needed.
Qualifications:
  • Bachelor’s degree in nonprofit management, social work, human resources, education, or related degree. Additional experience may be substituted for degree requirement.
  • 1-2 years experience in volunteer and/or visitor services, or equivalent public-facing capacity to perform such responsibilities.
  • Demonstrated ability (or clearly demonstrated capacity) to effectively work with volunteers.
  • Must possess a valid Massachusetts driver’s license that is in good standing at time of appointment and for duration of employment.
  • Must be able to work outside in all types of weather and bend, stoop, reach, lift, and carry up to 50 lbs. as necessary to carry out duties.
  • Exceptional organizational and problem-solving skills, with strong attention to detail and follow-through.
  • Experience handling and prioritizing a variety of responsibilities simultaneously.
  • Commitment to always interact with diverse arrays of colleagues and park users courteously and professionally.
  • Fluency with Microsoft office suite and related programs.
  • Multilingual fluency is a plus.
  • Passion for parks, recreation, and open space is strongly encouraged!
Logistics:
  • Work hours are on average 40 hours per week, currently Monday through Friday 9a-5pm with infrequent, predetermined weekend commitments. When the Esplanade Smith Family Pavilion and Charlesbank Campus opens, work hours will be on average 40 hours per week Tuesday – Saturday 8a-4p. Work hours/days might vary periodically based on volunteer program needs. Prepare for significant variance around the exciting time period of the grand opening, which may require changes for additional evening, weekend, or early morning hours.
  • Must be available to support some volunteer work on periodic nights, weekends, and some holidays.
  • Work will require being in both indoor and outdoor settings across seasons.
  • Applicants are subject to Criminal Offender Record Information (C.O.R.I) check, however, we believe in rehabilitation and will provide any applicant the opportunity to address past work and life experiences.
Compensation:
  • EA offers a competitive salary for the Boston non-profit and parks sector. Performance and compensation are reviewed regularly, and management provides all employees with transparent benchmarks and paths for professional development and promotion within the organization. The annual salary range for this position will be $50,000-60,000, commensurate with prior experience and demonstrated skills.
Benefits:
  • 15 vacation, 12 sick & 2 personal days per year (after 2 years of service, vacation days increase to 17)
  • 11 holidays. Thanksgiving, Christmas, New Year’s Day, MLK Day, and Presidents’ Day off and the 6 remaining (Memorial Day, Juneteenth, July 4, Labor Day, Indigenous Peoples’ Day, and Veterans’ Day) as floating holidays depending on the holiday worked.
  • Health and dental insurance, 80% of monthly premium paid by EA
  • Health savings account with $2,000 EA contribution for those enrolled in EA health plan
  • 403(b) retirement plan
  • Commuter benefits, pre-tax deduction up to $300/month
  • Paid professional development opportunities
Application Process:
  • Please submit your resume and cover letter
  • Demonstrate the quality of your written communications and strong case-making by responding to this question in your cover letter: Why is stewardship of public parks a great platform for volunteerism?
  • No phone calls, please.
The Esplanade Association is an Equal Opportunity Employer and greatly encourages candidates of all backgrounds to apply. Diversity of opinions, experiences, and backgrounds is a key and valued component of our work to promote a welcoming, accessible, and inclusive experience on the Esplanade through an organization that is itself diverse and inclusive.
Not sure you meet 100% of our qualifications? Research shows that men apply for jobs when they meet an average of 60% of the criteria. Yet, women and other people who are systematically marginalized tend to only apply if they meet every requirement. If you believe that you could excel in this role, we encourage you to apply. We are dedicated to considering a broad array of candidates, including those with diverse workplace experiences and backgrounds. Whether you’re new to non-profit administration, returning to work after a gap in employment, simply looking to transition, or take the next step in your career path, we will be glad to have you on our radar. Please use your cover letter to tell us about your interest and what you hope to bring to this role.

title: Senior Incident Response Analyst
description:
At Leidos, we deliver innovative solutions through the efforts of our diverse and talented people who are dedicated to our customers’ success. We empower our teams, contribute to our communities, and operate sustainable. Everything we do is built on a commitment to do the right thing for our customers, our people, and our community. Our Mission, Vision, and Values guide the way we do business.

If this sounds like the kind of environment where you can thrive, keep reading!

The Digital Modernization Sector brings together our digital transformation and IT programs, allowing us to better serve our customers through scale and repeatability. Leidos has a critical need for a Senior Incident Response Analyst to support the DHS CISA Program.

The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Security Operations Center (SOC) Support Services is a US Government program responsible to monitor, detect, analyze, mitigate, and respond to cyber threats and adversarial activity on the DHS Enterprise. The DHS SOC has primary responsibility for monitoring and responding to security events and incidents detected at the Trusted Internet Connection (TIC) and Policy Enforcement Point (PEP) and is responsible for directing and coordinating detection and response activities performed by each Component SOC. Direction and coordination are achieved through a new shared DHS incident tracking system and other means of coordination and communication. Leidos is seeking a Senior Incident Response Analyst to join our team on this highly visible DHS CISA SOC Program.

The Incident Responder will perform the following:

• Coordinate investigation and response efforts throughout the Incident Response lifecycle

• Correlate and and analyze events and data to determine scope of Cyber Incidents

• Acquire and analyze endpoint and network artifacts, volatile memory, malicious files/binaries and scripts

• Recognize attacker tactics, techniques, and procedures as potential indicators of compromise (IOCs) that can be used to improve monitoring, analysis and Incident Response.

• Develop, document, and maintain Incident Response process, procedures, workflows, and playbooks

• Tune and maintain security tools (EDR, IDS, SIEM, etc) to reduce false positives and improve SOC detection capabilities

• Document Investigation and Incident Response actions taken in Case Management Systems and prepare formal Incident Reports

• Create metrics and determine Key Performance Indicators to drive maturity of SOC operations

• Develop security content such as scripts, signatures, and alerts

Basic Qualifications

Bachelors’ degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Technology, Cyber Security, or related field and 12-15 years of related experience. Additional years of experience and/or cyber certifications may be considered in lieu of degree.

In-depth knowledge of each phase of the Incident Response life cycle

• Expertise of Operating Systems (Windows/Linux) operations and artifacts

• Expertise of Enterprise Network Architectures to include routing/switching, common protocols (DHCP, DNS, HTTP, etc), and devices (Firewalls, Proxies, Load Balancers, VPN, etc)

• Ability to recognize suspicious activity/events, common attacker TTPs, and perform logical analysis and research to determine root cause and scope of Incidents

• Expertise with Cyber Kill Chain and have utilized the ATT&CK Framework

• Have scripting experience with Python, PowerShell, and/or Bash

• Ability to independently prioritize and complete multiple tasks with little to no supervision

• Flexible and adaptable self-starter with strong relationship-building skills

• Strong problem-solving abilities with an analytic and qualitative eye for reasoning

• Strong verbal and written communication skills

•Ability to communicate with all levels of audiences (subordinates, peers & leadership)

* Candidate must have technical hands on experience in the areas of incident detection and response, malware analysis, or computer forensics.

All Department of Homeland Security SOC employees are required to favorably pass a 5-year (BI) Background Investigation.

Candidates will have at least one of the following certifications:

SANS GIAC: GCIH, GCIA, GCFA, GPEN GCFE, GREM

CISSP OSCP, OSCE, OSWP

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in cyber government, and/or federal law enforcement FISMA systems.

title: Automotive Lube Tech
description:
We're growing and we'd love to have you grow with us

Atlantic Coast Enterprises is seeking to hire part-time and full-time Automotive Technicians to provide top-notch service at a Jiffy Lube in Lakeland, FL. Are you looking to learn and advance your skills with a company that cares about its employees? Do you want to work in a collaborative, positive environment where humor, teamwork, and laughter are encouraged? If so, keep reading!

Our Automotive Technicians/Auto Mechanics earn a salary of up to $40,000 per year based on experience. We also offer generous benefits including paid vacation after one year of employment, longevity bonuses, comprehensive health care, dental/vision insurance, basic life insurance, short-term disability, long-term disability, a 401(k) plan, bereavement leave, and employee oil changes and discounts. If this sounds like the right part-time or full-time position for you, apply today!

ABOUT ATLANTIC COAST ENTERPRISES

Atlantic Coast Enterprises (ACE) is a full-service lubrication, fluid, and automotive maintenance center. We offer our customers these services in the cleanest, most professional surroundings possible. Each day we strive to achieve our mission to create customers for life through fast, friendly, clean, and professional service. We are dedicated to expanding and moving constantly on to new and different challenges. A few short years ago, we were recognized as the franchisee of the year within the Jiffy Lube nationwide network.

Everything at ACE is a team effort. We know that without our employees we wouldn't be able to grow, improve, or create lifelong customers. This is why we offer competitive compensation, generous benefits, and a supportive, collaborative environment. We encourage each and every employee to share their ideas with us.

A DAY IN THE LIFE OF A LUBE TECH

You arrive each day determined to take excellent care of our customers. They trust your competence, as well as your integrity to keep their vehicles running. Utilizing the training we have provided, you are able to correctly identify mechanical problems, provide preventative maintenance, and carefully address customer concerns. With your excellent communication skills, you give recommendations for repairs along with proper labor and time estimates. You then make the repairs and replace parts as requested. Your positive attitude and ability to stay on top of the latest knowledge and training ensure your success!

QUALIFICATIONS

  • At least 18 years old
  • Valid driver's license
  • Physical ability to perform typical tasks required for repairing and servicing vehicles including the ability to stand for several hours at a time and lift up to 50 lbs
  • Comfortable working in a variety of weather conditions

No experience? Don't worry! We will teach you everything you need to know. Any previous experience is a plus! Do you have excellent mechanical skills and the drive to problem-solve? Are you able to work independently and in a team environment? Do you have exceptional customer service skills? If so, you may be perfect for this part-time or full-time position!

WORK SCHEDULE

Our Lube Techs work anywhere from 15-40 hours/week depending on part-time or full-time status. The typical work schedule varies during our business hours and will include a mix of day, evening, and weekend shifts--but no late nights. We are open 8am to 7pm Monday-Saturday and 9am to 4pm on Sunday.

ARE YOU READY TO JOIN OUR TEAM?

If you feel that you are right for this position, apply now with our initial 3-minute, mobile-friendly application.

Professional Nanny

Join the Five Star Companion Care Team

At Five Star Companion Care, we believe exceptional childcare begins with exceptional caregivers. We are seeking experienced, compassionate, and career-minded Professional Nannies to provide high-quality, in-home childcare for families throughout Philadelphia, Montgomery, Delaware, Chester, and Bucks Counties.

We are looking for individuals who view nannying as a profession—not simply a job—and who are committed to creating safe, nurturing, and engaging environments where children can learn, grow, and thrive.

If you are dependable, professional, and passionate about making a positive impact in the lives of children and families, we invite you to apply.

Benefits & Perks

  • Competitive Pay

  • Flexible Scheduling

  • Career Advancement Opportunities

  • Supportive Team Environment

  • Rewarding Career with Professional Growth

Responsibilities

  • Provide attentive, age-appropriate care for infants, toddlers, and school-aged children

  • Plan educational, creative, and recreational activities

  • Prepare healthy meals and snacks

  • Assist with homework and developmental learning

  • Maintain children's daily routines

  • Perform light housekeeping related to the children

  • Transport children to and from school, activities, and appointments when required

  • Maintain a safe, clean, and nurturing home environment

  • Communicate professionally with parents regarding the children's daily activities and progress

  • Maintain confidentiality and professionalism in every family's home

Qualifications

  • Minimum one (1) year of paid childcare experience caring for children who are not family members (required)

  • Must be available to work some evenings and weekends

  • High School Diploma or GED required

  • Reliable transportation required

  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills

  • Professional appearance and positive attitude

  • Dependable, trustworthy, patient, and compassionate

How to Apply

To be considered for a position, upload the following:

  • Professional resume

  • Cover letter explaining:

    • Why you chose nannying as your career.

    • What makes you an exceptional nanny.

    • Why you would like to join the Five Star Companion Care team.

  • One recent, high-quality photo of yourself. This may be:

    • A professional headshot, or

    • A recent, clear photo that reflects your personality and professionalism.

Photo Guidelines

  • Taken within the last 12 months

  • Clear, well-lit, and front-facing

  • No filters or heavy photo editing

  • No sunglasses or hats that obscure your face

  • Appropriate for a professional childcare position

Your photo helps us get to know you and supports our personalized matching process with families.

Qualified applicants will be contacted to schedule an in-person interview.

Pre-Employment Requirements

Final candidates must successfully complete the following before hire:

  • Pennsylvania State Police Criminal History Check (PATCH)

  • Pennsylvania Child Abuse History Clearance

  • FBI Fingerprint Clearance (if required)

  • Current TB Screening (2-Step PPD or QuantiFERON®-TB Gold Blood Test)

Why Five Star Companion Care?

At Five Star Companion Care, we carefully match professional nannies with families seeking dependable, trustworthy, and compassionate childcare. Our commitment to professionalism, personalized matching, and exceptional service allows us to build lasting relationships with the families we serve.

If you're ready to build a rewarding career with an agency that values excellence, professionalism, and compassion, we encourage you to apply today.

Five Star Companion Care
Where Compassion Comes First.
